title.zh: 卷六十一 列傳第四十九: 王盟 獨孤信 竇熾 賀蘭祥 叱列伏龜 閻慶 史寧 權景宣
title.en: Volume 61 Biographies 49: Wang Meng, Du Guxin, Dou Chi, He Lanxiang, Chilie Fugui, Yan Qing, Shi Ning, Quan Jingxuan
title.raw: 卷六十一 列傳第四十九: 王盟 獨孤信 竇熾 賀蘭祥 叱列伏龜 閻慶 史寧 權景宣 Volume 61 Biographies 49: Wang Meng, Du Guxin, Dou Chi, He Lanxiang, Chilie Fugui, Yan Qing, Shi Ning, Quan Jingxuan

sentences.zh: 王盟 獨孤信 竇熾 賀蘭祥 叱列伏龜 閻慶 史寧 權景宣

translations.literal: Wang Meng, Dugu Xin, Dou Chi, Helan Xiang, Chiliefu Gui, Yan Qing, Shi Ning, Quan Jingxuan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, Dugu Xin, Dou Chi, Helan Xiang, Chiliefu Gui, Yan Qing, Shi Ning, and Quan Jingxuan

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十九

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Forty-Nine
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 49

sentences.zh: 王盟子勱從孫誼獨孤信子羅竇熾兄子榮定毅賀蘭祥叱列伏龜閻慶子毗史寧子雄祥權景宣

translations.literal: Wang Meng, his son Bo, his grand-nephew Yi; Dugu Xin, his son Luo; Dou Chi, his brother's son Rongding Yi; Helan Xiang; Chiliefu Gui; Yan Qing, his son Pi; Shi Ning, his son Xiongxiang; Quan Jingxuan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, his son Bo, and his grand-nephew Yi; Dugu Xin and his son Luo; Dou Chi and his brother's son Rongding Yi; Helan Xiang; Chiliefu Gui; Yan Qing and his son Pi; Shi Ning and his son Xiongxiang; and Quan Jingxuan

sentences.zh: 王盟，字仵，明德皇后之兄也，其先樂浪人。

translations.literal: Wang Meng, courtesy name Wu, was the elder brother of Empress Mingde; his ancestors were men of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, courtesy name Wu, was the elder brother of Empress Mingde. His family originally came from Lelang.

sentences.zh: 六世祖波，前燕太宰。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Bo was Grand Minister of Former Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Bo had served as Grand Minister under Former Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖珍，魏黃門侍郎，贈并州刺史、樂浪公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate of Wei, posthumously granted Governor of Bing Province and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had been a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate under Wei and was posthumously granted the title of Governor of Bing Province and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 父羆，伏波將軍，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Pi was General Who Quells the Waves; as a son of a good family he garrisoned Wuchuan and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi was General Who Quells the Waves. Posted to Wuchuan as a soldier from a respectable family, he settled there and made it the family home.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，破六韓拔陵攻陷諸鎮，盟亦為其所擁。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, Poliuhan Baling captured the garrison towns, and Meng was also taken into his ranks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era of Wei, when Poliuhan Baling overran the frontier garrisons, Meng was swept up into his forces as well.

sentences.zh: 拔陵平後，流寓中山，復以積射將軍從蕭寶夤西征。

translations.literal: After Baling was suppressed, he drifted to Zhongshan and again followed Xiao Baoyin west on campaign as General of Accumulated Archers.
translations.idiomatic: After Baling's rebellion was put down, Meng wandered to Zhongshan and later joined Xiao Baoyin's western campaign as General of Accumulated Archers.

sentences.zh: 寶夤僭逆，盟遂逃匿人間。

translations.literal: When Baoyin usurped power, Meng then fled and hid among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled and seized power, Meng went into hiding among the common people.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃天光入關，盟從之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang entered the passes, Meng followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang marched into the Guanzhong region, Meng joined his cause.

sentences.zh: 隋賀拔岳禽萬俊志願奴，平秦隴，常先登力戰。

translations.literal: Following Helba Yue, he captured Wan Jun Zhiyuan Nu and pacified Qin and Long, often being first to ascend and fight with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Helba Yue, he helped capture Wan Jun Zhiyuan Nu and pacify Qin and Long, repeatedly leading the charge in the fiercest fighting.

sentences.zh: 及周文帝平侯莫陳悅，除盟原州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou suppressed Houmochen Yue, Meng was appointed Governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Zhou defeated Houmochen Yue, Meng was appointed Governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 孝武至長安，封魏昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu arrived at Chang'an, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weichang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang'an, Meng was enfeoffed as Duke of Weichang County.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，徵拜司空，轉司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Works, then transferred to Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, he was summoned to court and appointed Minister of Works, then promoted to Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 迎文帝悼後於蠕蠕，加侍中，遷太尉。

translations.literal: Welcoming Empress Daohou of Emperor Wen from the Rouran, he was additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After escorting Emperor Wen's consort Empress Daohou back from the Rouran, he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant and then promoted to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝東征，以留後大都督行雍州事，節度關中諸軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei marched east, he was made Rear-Area Grand Commander administering Yong Province and directing all armies in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei marched east on campaign, Meng was left behind as Grand Commander administering Yong Province and directing all military forces in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 趙青雀之亂，盟與開府李虎輔太子出頓渭北。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Zhao Qingque, Meng and the Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Hu escorted the crown prince out to encamp north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhao Qingque's rebellion, Meng and Li Hu, Director of the Department of State Affairs, escorted the crown prince to a camp north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 事平，進長樂郡公，賜姓拓王氏。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was advanced to Duke of Changle Commandery and granted the surname Tuo-Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crisis was resolved, he was promoted to Duke of Changle Commandery and granted the surname Tuo-Wang.

sentences.zh: 遷太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 九年，進位太傅，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was advanced to Grand Preceptor and additionally given the status of Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and additionally granted the ceremonial rank of Director of the Department of State Affairs, equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 盟姿度弘雅，仁而汎愛。

translations.literal: Meng's bearing was broad and refined, and he was benevolent and universally loving.
translations.idiomatic: Meng carried himself with broad, refined dignity and was benevolent and warmly generous to all.

sentences.zh: 雖居師傅，禮冠群後，而謙恭自處，未嘗以勢位驕人。

translations.literal: Although he held the rank of tutor and his ceremonial precedence surpassed the other nobles, he conducted himself with humility and never used his power and position to act arrogantly toward others.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held the exalted rank of imperial tutor and took ceremonial precedence over the other nobles, he remained humble and never lorded his power and status over anyone.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝甚尊重之，及疾，數幸其第，親問所欲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei greatly respected him; when he fell ill, the emperor repeatedly visited his residence and personally asked what he desired.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei held him in the highest regard. When Meng fell ill, the emperor visited his home repeatedly and asked in person what he might wish for.

sentences.zh: 十一年，薨，贈本官，諡曰孝定。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he died; his existing offices were granted posthumously, and he was given the posthumous title Xiaoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died. His existing offices were confirmed posthumously, and he was given the posthumous name Xiaoding, "Filial and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 子勱，字醜興，性忠果有材幹。

translations.literal: His son Bo, courtesy name Chouxing, was by nature loyal, resolute, and talented.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bo, courtesy name Chouxing, was loyal and resolute by nature and possessed real ability.

sentences.zh: 年十七，從周文帝入關。

translations.literal: At age seventeen, he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou into the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 及平秦隴，定關中，周文嘗謂曰：「為將坐見成敗者上也，被堅執銳者次也。」

translations.literal: When Qin and Long were pacified and Guanzhong secured, Zhou Wen once said to him: "For a general, the highest is one who sits and sees victory and defeat; next is one who wears armor and wields sharp weapons."
translations.idiomatic: After Qin and Long were pacified and Guanzhong secured, Emperor Wen once told him, "The finest general is one who can read the tide of battle from his command post; the next best is the one who dons armor and takes up arms himself.

sentences.zh: 勱曰：「意欲兼被之。」

translations.literal: Bo said: "I intend to do both."
translations.idiomatic: Bo replied, "I mean to do both."

sentences.zh: 周文大笑。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 尋拜散騎常侍，賜爵梁甫縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and granted the title of Duke of Liangfu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangfu County.

sentences.zh: 大統初，為千牛備身直長，領左右，出入臥內，小心謹厚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he served as Chief of the Thousand-Ox Guard of the Body, commanding the Left and Right Guards, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters, careful, cautious, and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he served as Chief of the Thousand-Ox Guard of the Body, commanding the emperor's personal guard and attending him even in the inner chambers. He was careful, cautious, and utterly dependable.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝常曰：「王勱可謂不二心臣也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei often said: "Wang Bo may truly be called a minister of undivided loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei often said, "Wang Bo is a minister whose loyalty never wavers.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，勱以都督領禁兵，居左翼，當其前者死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: In the battle of Shayuan, Bo as Commander led the forbidden troops on the left wing; those who faced the enemy ahead of him suffered heavy casualties.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Shayuan, Bo commanded the imperial guard on the left wing. The men who stood in the path of the enemy ahead of him suffered terrible losses.

sentences.zh: 勱亦被傷重，遂卒於行間。

translations.literal: Bo was also severely wounded and thus died on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Bo himself was gravely wounded and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 周文深悼焉。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、太尉、尚書令、十州諸軍事、雍州刺史，追封咸陽郡公，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Commander of Military Affairs in Ten Provinces, and Governor of Yong Province; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xianyang Commandery; posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Commander of Military Affairs in Ten Provinces, and Governor of Yong Province, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xianyang Commandery with the posthumous name Zhongwu, "Loyal and Martial."

sentences.zh: 子弼襲爵，尚魏安樂公主，位大都督、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Bi inherited the title, married Princess Anle of Wei, and held the positions of Grand Commander and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi inherited the title, married Princess Anle of Wei, and served as Grand Commander and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 子悅嗣，位大將軍、同州刺史，改封濟南郡公。

translations.literal: His son Yue succeeded, held the positions of Grand General and Governor of Tong Province, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jinan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue succeeded to the line, served as Grand General and Governor of Tong Province, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jinan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 盟兄子顯，幼而敏悟，沉靜少言。

translations.literal: Meng's elder brother's son Xian was clever and perceptive from childhood, calm and quiet, and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's nephew Xian, the son of his elder brother, was bright and perceptive from childhood, calm and reserved, and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 初為周文帳內都督，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、光祿卿、鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was a Commander within Zhou Wen's tent guard, and was repeatedly promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, Minister of Imperial Brightness, and Governor of Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commander in Emperor Wen's personal guard and rose through the ranks to General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Minister of Imperial Brightness, and Governor of Feng Province.

sentences.zh: 賜爵洛邑縣公，進位大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: Granted the title of Duke of Luoyi County, advanced to Grand General, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Luoyi County, promoted to Grand General, and later died.

sentences.zh: 子誼。

translations.literal: His son was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi.

sentences.zh: 誼字宜君，少有大志，便弓馬，博覽群言。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Yijun, from youth had great ambition, was skilled with bow and horse, and broadly read many works.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Yijun, had lofty ambitions from youth. He was skilled in archery and horsemanship and read widely across many fields of learning.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝時，為左中侍上士。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Min of Zhou, he served as Senior Attendant of the Left Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Min of Zhou, he served as Senior Attendant of the Left Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 時大塚宰宇文護執政，帝拱默無所關預。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held power, and the emperor remained silent and had no part in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held real power, and the emperor remained silent and took no part in governing.

sentences.zh: 有朝士於帝側微不恭，誼勃然而進，將擊之，其人惶懼請罪，乃止。

translations.literal: A court official at the emperor's side was slightly disrespectful; Yi suddenly advanced in anger and was about to strike him; the man, fearful, begged forgiveness, and Yi stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When a court official beside the emperor showed slight disrespect, Yi surged forward in anger and was about to strike him. The man, terrified, begged forgiveness, and Yi relented.

sentences.zh: 自是朝臣無敢不肅。

translations.literal: From then on no court official dared fail to be reverent.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no court official dared show anything but the utmost deference.

sentences.zh: 遷禦正大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Imperial Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Imperial Rectitude.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，毀瘁過禮，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death, his grief exceeded the rites; he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, his grief exceeded what the rites required. He built a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth by hand to complete the burial mound.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，鄖州總管司馬消難舉兵反，帝以誼為行軍元帥討之，未至而消難奔陳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, the Area Commander of Ying Province Sima Xiaonan raised troops in rebellion; the emperor appointed Yi as Campaign Commander to suppress him, but before Yi arrived Xiaonan fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still Chancellor, Sima Xiaonan, Area Commander of Ying Province, rose in rebellion. The emperor appointed Yi as Campaign Commander to suppress him, but before Yi arrived Xiaonan had already fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 于時北至商、洛，南拒江、淮，東西二千餘里，巴蠻多叛，共推渠帥蘭洛州為主。

translations.literal: At that time from Shang and Luo in the north to the Yangtze and Huai in the south, more than two thousand li east and west, many Ba tribes rebelled and jointly made the chieftain Lan Luozhou their leader.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, from Shang and Luo in the north to the Yangtze and Huai in the south—a stretch of more than two thousand li east to west—many Ba tribes rebelled and together made the chieftain Lan Luozhou their leader.

sentences.zh: 洛州自號河南王以附消難，北連尉遲迥。

translations.literal: Luozhou styled himself King of Henan to join Xiaonan and linked with Yuchi Tong in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou proclaimed himself King of Henan and joined Xiaonan's cause, while in the north he linked up with Yuchi Tong.

sentences.zh: 誼分兵討之，旬月皆平。

translations.literal: Yi divided his troops to suppress them, and within a month all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yi divided his forces to suppress the rebels, and within a month had pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使勞問，冠蓋不絕，以第五女妻其子奉孝。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys with congratulations; official carriages came in an unbroken stream, and he gave his fifth daughter in marriage to Yi's son Fengxiao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to congratulate him in an unbroken stream of official visits, and gave his fifth daughter in marriage to Yi's son Fengxiao.

sentences.zh: 尋拜大司徒。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 誼自以與帝有舊，亦歸心焉。

translations.literal: Yi, considering himself to have old ties with the emperor, also gave him his wholehearted loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, believing himself to share a long friendship with the emperor, gave him his wholehearted loyalty as well.

sentences.zh: 及隋受禪，顧遇彌厚，帝親幸其第，與之極歡。

translations.literal: When Sui received the abdication, his favor grew ever greater; the emperor personally visited his residence and shared the greatest conviviality with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui dynasty was founded, the emperor's favor toward him grew even deeper. The emperor visited his home in person and they shared the warmest companionship.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蘇威議，以為戶口滋多，人田不贍，欲減功臣之地以給人。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Su Wei proposed that as registered households increased and people's fields could not support them, he wished to reduce the lands of meritorious officials to give to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Su Wei proposed that as the population grew and commoners' fields could no longer sustain them, the lands granted to meritorious officials should be reduced and reallocated to the people.

sentences.zh: 誼奏曰：「百官者，曆世勳賢，方蒙爵土，一旦削之，未見其可。」

translations.literal: Yi memorialized, saying: "The hundred officials are meritorious worthies across generations who have just received noble titles and lands; to cut them off at once—I do not see how that can be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial saying, "These officials are meritorious servants of the dynasty who have only just received titles and fiefs. To strip them away all at once—I cannot see how that would be right.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，竟寢威議。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and ultimately shelved Wei's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and in the end Su Wei's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 帝將幸岐州，諫曰：「陛下初臨萬國，人情未洽，何用此行。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to visit Qi Province, Yi remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty has only just come to rule the myriad states; popular sentiment is not yet settled—what need is there for this journey?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a visit to Qi Province, Yi remonstrated, "Your Majesty has only just ascended to rule the realm. The people's hearts are not yet fully won—what purpose would this journey serve?

sentences.zh: 上戲之曰：「吾昔與公位望齊等，一朝屈節為臣，或當恥愧，是行也，振揚威武，欲以服公心耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor joked with him, saying: "In the past you and I were equal in rank and standing; in one morning you bent your will to become a subject—perhaps you feel shame. This journey is to display martial authority and make you submit in heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor teased him, saying, "You and I were once equals in rank and standing. Now you have bent your will to serve as my subject—perhaps that still stings. This journey is meant to display imperial might and win your wholehearted submission."

sentences.zh: 誼笑而退。

translations.literal: Yi smiled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yi smiled and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋奉使突厥。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent on mission to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dispatched on a mission to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其稱旨，進郢國公。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his fulfillment of the imperial intent and advanced him to Duke of Ying State.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for carrying out the mission to his satisfaction and promoted him to Duke of Ying State.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其子奉孝卒。

translations.literal: Before long, his son Fengxiao died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his son Fengxiao died.

sentences.zh: 逾年，誼上表言公主少，請除服。

translations.literal: After a year, Yi submitted a memorial saying the princess was young and requesting removal of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yi submitted a memorial saying the princess was still young and asking that she be released from mourning.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫楊素劾誼曰：「臣聞喪服有五，親疏異節；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yang Su impeached Yi, saying: "I have heard that mourning garments are of five kinds, with different periods according to closeness of kin;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yang Su impeached Yi, saying, "I have heard that there are five grades of mourning garments, each with its own period according to the closeness of kinship;

sentences.zh: 喪制有四，降殺殊文。

translations.literal: mourning regulations are of four kinds, with descending gradations and differing forms.
translations.idiomatic: and that mourning regulations fall into four categories, each with descending gradations and its own prescribed form.

sentences.zh: 王者之所常行，故曰不易之道也。

translations.literal: These are what rulers constantly observe, and are therefore called the unchanging Way.
translations.idiomatic: These are what rulers are bound to observe, and are therefore called the unchanging Way.

sentences.zh: 而儀同王奉孝既尚蘭陵公主，以去年五月身喪，始經一周，而誼便請除釋。

translations.literal: Yet Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Fengxiao, having married Princess Lanling, suffered bereavement last May; only one full cycle has passed, yet Yi has already requested removal of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Fengxiao, a Director of the Department of State Affairs, having married Princess Lanling, lost his wife last May. Only one full year of mourning has passed, and already Yi has asked that she be released from it.

sentences.zh: 竊以雖曰王姬，終成下嫁之禮；

translations.literal: I venture to think that although she is called a royal princess, in the end the rites of marriage to a lower house apply;
translations.idiomatic: I would submit that although she is a royal princess, in the end the rites of marriage into a subject's household still apply;

sentences.zh: 公則主之，猶在移天之義。

translations.literal: as for the duke, he is her lord, and the principle of shifting heaven's authority still applies.
translations.idiomatic: and as for the duke, he remains her lord, and the principle that a wife's mourning follows her husband's house still holds.

sentences.zh: 況復三年之喪，自上達下，及期釋服，在禮未詳。

translations.literal: Moreover, for the three-year mourning, from those above down to those below, release from garments at the end of the period—the rites are not clear on this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for three-year mourning, from the highest to the lowest, release from mourning garments at the end of the prescribed period is nowhere clearly defined in the rites.

sentences.zh: 然夫婦之則，人倫攸始，喪紀之制，人道至大，苟不重之，取笑君子。

translations.literal: Yet the rule between husband and wife is where human relations begin; the regulations of mourning are the greatest of human conduct—if one does not honor them, one invites the ridicule of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between husband and wife is where human relations begin, and mourning regulations are among the greatest obligations of human conduct. To treat them lightly is to invite the scorn of all right-minded men.

sentences.zh: 故鑽燧改火，責以居喪之速；

translations.literal: Therefore when drilling flint and changing fire, one is reproached for the speed of dwelling in mourning;
translations.idiomatic: That is why Zengzi was rebuked for changing mourning fires too soon—he had ended his mourning too quickly;

sentences.zh: 朝祥暮歌，譏以忘哀之早。

translations.literal: singing in the morning at the end-of-mourning sacrifice and in the evening—one is mocked for forgetting grief too early.
translations.idiomatic: and why Yan Yuan was mocked for singing at dawn on the day of the end-of-mourning sacrifice and again at dusk—he had forgotten his grief too soon.

sentences.zh: 然誼雖不自強，爵位已重，欲為無禮，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Yet although Yi may not force the issue himself, his rank and position are already weighty—wishing to act without propriety, how can that be permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Yi may not be forcing the issue himself, but his rank and position are already exalted. To seek exemption from propriety—how can that be permitted?

sentences.zh: 乃薄俗傷教，為父則不慈；

translations.literal: This is shallow custom that injures teaching—as a father he is unkind;
translations.idiomatic: This is vulgar custom that corrupts moral teaching: as a father he shows no kindness;

sentences.zh: 輕禮易喪，致婦於無義。

translations.literal: treating rites lightly and changing mourning easily, he brings his daughter-in-law to be without righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: by treating the rites lightly and shortening mourning, he leaves his daughter-in-law without righteousness.

sentences.zh: 若縱而不正，恐傷風俗。」

translations.literal: If this is indulged and not corrected, I fear it will harm custom and mores."
translations.idiomatic: If this is indulged and not corrected, I fear it will damage public morals.

sentences.zh: 有詔不問。

translations.literal: An edict was issued not to pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued directing that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 然恩禮稍薄，誼頗怨望。

translations.literal: Yet imperial favor and courtesy gradually grew thinner, and Yi became quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet imperial favor toward him gradually cooled, and Yi grew increasingly resentful.

sentences.zh: 或告誼謀反，帝令案其事。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yi was plotting rebellion; the emperor ordered an investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Yi was plotting rebellion, and the emperor ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 主者奏誼有不遜之言，實無反狀。

translations.literal: The responsible official reported that Yi had disrespectful words but in fact no signs of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating officials reported that Yi had spoken disrespectfully but showed no actual signs of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝賜酒而釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him wine and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him wine and released him.

sentences.zh: 時上柱國元諧亦頗失意，誼數與往來，言論醜惡。

translations.literal: At that time the Pillar of the State Yuan Xie was also quite discontented; Yi frequently associated with him, and their talk was ugly and vile.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Xie, a Pillar of the State, was also deeply discontented. Yi frequently associated with him, and their conversations were ugly and seditious.

sentences.zh: 胡僧告之。

translations.literal: A Hu monk reported them.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk reported them.

sentences.zh: 公卿奏誼大逆不道，罪當死。

translations.literal: The high officials reported that Yi's great treason and unfilial conduct warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: The high officials reported that Yi's treason and unfilial conduct warranted death.

sentences.zh: 帝見誼，愴然曰：「朕與公舊同學，甚相憐憫，將奈國法何。」

translations.literal: The emperor saw Yi and said sorrowfully: "You and I were old schoolmates; I pity you greatly—what can I do about the laws of the state?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw Yi, he said sorrowfully, "You and I were old schoolmates, and my heart goes out to you—but what can I do against the laws of the state?

sentences.zh: 於是詔曰：「誼有周之世，早預人倫，朕共遊庠序，遂相親好。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict said: "Yi, in the time of Zhou, early entered human relations; I studied with him at the academy and thus became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict declared, "In the time of Zhou, Yi and I entered society together. We studied at the same academy and became close friends.

sentences.zh: 然性懷險薄，巫覡盈門，鬼言怪語，稱神道。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was treacherous and shallow; shamans and diviners filled his gates; ghost talk and strange words claimed the divine Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was treacherous and shallow. Shamans and diviners filled his household, and ghostly talk and strange prophecies claimed the authority of the divine Way.

sentences.zh: 朕受命之初，深存戒約，口雲改悔，心實不悛。

translations.literal: At the beginning when I received the Mandate, I deeply admonished and restrained him; his mouth said he would reform, but in heart he truly did not repent.
translations.idiomatic: When I first received the Mandate, I warned and restrained him deeply. His mouth promised repentance, but his heart never truly changed.

sentences.zh: 乃說四天王神道，誼應受命，書有誼讖，天有誼星，桃、鹿二川，岐州之下，歲在辰巳，興帝王之業。

translations.literal: He spoke of the divine Way of the Four Heavenly Kings, that Yi should receive the Mandate; writings contained prophecies about Yi, heaven had a star of Yi; at the Peach and Deer Rivers below Qi Province, in the years of chen and si, he would raise an emperor's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of the divine Way of the Four Heavenly Kings and claimed that Yi was destined to receive the Mandate. Prophecies in writing named Yi; heaven held a star named for Yi. At the Peach and Deer Rivers below Qi Province, in the years of chen and si, he would raise an imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 密令卜問，伺殿省之災。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered divination and watched for calamities in the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered divinations and watched for calamities in the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 又說其身是明王聖主。

translations.literal: He also said that his own person was a bright king and sage lord.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared that he himself was a bright king and sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 信用左道，所在詿誤。

translations.literal: Trusting heterodox ways, wherever he went he led people astray.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting heterodox practices, he led people astray wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 自言相表，當王不疑。

translations.literal: He said of his own physiognomy that he was destined to be king without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his own physiognomy, he declared that he was destined to become king without doubt.

sentences.zh: 此而赦之，將或為亂。

translations.literal: If this man is pardoned, he may yet cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If such a man is pardoned, he may yet bring about rebellion.

sentences.zh: 禁暴除惡，宜伏國刑。」

translations.literal: To restrain violence and remove evil, he should submit to the state's punishment."
translations.idiomatic: To restrain violence and root out evil, he should submit to the punishment of the state."

sentences.zh: 帝復令大理正趙綽謂誼曰：「時命如此，將若之何！」

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered the Chief Judge of the Court of Justice Zhao Chuo to say to Yi: "Fate is such—what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Zhao Chuo, Chief Judge of the Court of Justice, to tell Yi, "Such is fate—what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 乃賜死于家，時年四十六。

translations.literal: He was then granted death at home; he was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted death at home, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信，雲中人也，本名如願。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin was a man of Yunzhong; his original name was Ruyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin was a native of Yunzhong. His original name was Ruyuan.

sentences.zh: 魏初有四十六部，其先伏留屯者為部落大人，與魏俱起。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei there were forty-six tribes; his ancestors who settled at Fuliutun were tribal chieftains and rose together with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Wei there were forty-six tribal divisions. His ancestors, who had settled at Fuliutun, served as tribal chieftains and rose to power together with the Wei state.

sentences.zh: 祖俟尼，和平中，以良家子自雲中鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sini, in the Heping era, as a son of a good family garrisoned Wuchuan from Yunzhong and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sini, during the Heping era, was posted from Yunzhong to garrison Wuchuan as a soldier from a respectable family and settled there.

sentences.zh: 父庫者，為領人酋長，少雄豪有節義，北州咸敬服之。

translations.literal: His father Kuze was a tribal chieftain leader; from youth he was bold and heroic with a sense of honor, and all of the northern provinces respected and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuze was a tribal chieftain. Bold and heroic from youth and possessed of a strong sense of honor, he was respected and obeyed throughout the northern provinces.

sentences.zh: 信美容儀，善騎射。

translations.literal: Xin had a handsome appearance and was skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was handsome in bearing and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 正光末，與賀拔度等同斬衛可瑰，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, together with Helba Du and others he beheaded Wei Kei, and thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, he and Helba Du and others jointly beheaded Wei Kei, and thereby won renown.

sentences.zh: 後為葛榮所獲。

translations.literal: Later he was captured by Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later captured by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 信既少年，自修飾服章，軍中號為獨孤郎。

translations.literal: Since Xin was still young, he took care to adorn himself and his dress; in the army he was called Young Master Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: Still a young man, he took care with his appearance and dress, and in the army he was known as Young Master Dugu.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃氏破葛榮，以信為別將。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan defeated Ge Rong, Xin was made a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan defeated Ge Rong, Xin was appointed a separate commander.

sentences.zh: 從征韓婁，信匹馬挑戰，禽賊漁陽王袁肆周。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Han Lou, Xin challenged the enemy alone on horseback and captured the bandit Prince of Yuyang, Yuan Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Han Lou, Xin challenged the enemy alone on horseback and captured the bandit Prince of Yuyang, Yuan Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 後以破元顥黨，賜爵受德縣侯，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later for defeating the faction of Yuan Hao, he was granted the title of Marquis of Shoude County and transferred to General of the Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in defeating the faction of Yuan Hao, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shoude County and promoted to General of the Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝出鎮荊州，乃表信為大都督。

translations.literal: When Helba Sheng went out to garrison Jing Province, he memorialized the throne recommending Xin as Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Helba Sheng was posted to garrison Jing Province, he recommended Xin for appointment as Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 及勝弟岳為侯莫陳悅所害，勝乃令信入關，撫岳餘眾。

translations.literal: When Sheng's younger brother Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Sheng then ordered Xin to enter the passes and pacify Yue's remaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng's younger brother Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Sheng ordered Xin to enter the Guanzhong region and take command of Yue's remaining forces.

sentences.zh: 屬周文帝已統嶽兵，與信鄉里，少相友善，相見甚歡，因令信人洛請事。

translations.literal: By then Emperor Wen of Zhou had already taken command of Yue's army; he and Xin were from the same home region and had been friendly from youth; they were very glad to meet, and he therefore sent Xin to Luoyang to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Wen of Zhou had already assumed command of Yue's army. He and Xin came from the same region and had been friends since youth; delighted to see each other, he sent Xin to Luoyang to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 至雍州，大使元毗又遣信還荊州。

translations.literal: When he reached Yong Province, the Grand Ambassador Yuan Pi also sent Xin back to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yong Province, Grand Ambassador Yuan Pi sent him back to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 尋征入朝，魏孝武雅相委任。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to court, and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to court, and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，事起倉卒，信單騎及之於瀍澗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, the affair arose in haste; Xin rode alone and caught up with him at Chan Stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, the crisis erupted suddenly. Xin rode alone and caught up with him at Chan Stream.

sentences.zh: 孝武歎曰：「武衛遂能辭父母，捐妻子從我，世亂識忠良，豈虛言哉！」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sighed and said: "The Military Guard was able to leave his parents and abandon his wife and children to follow me—in chaotic times one recognizes the loyal and good; this is no empty saying!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sighed and said, "The Military Guard was able to leave his parents and abandon wife and children to follow me—in times of chaos one truly learns who is loyal. That is no empty saying!

sentences.zh: 進爵浮陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Fuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Fuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時荊州雖隱東魏，人心猶戀本朝，乃以信為衛大將軍、都督三荊州諸軍事，兼尚書右僕射、東南道行台、大都督、荊州刺史，以招懷之。

translations.literal: At that time although Jing Province was under Eastern Wei control, the people's hearts still yearned for the former dynasty; therefore Xin was made Grand General of the Guard, Commander of Military Affairs in the Three Jing Provinces, concurrently Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, Commissioner of the Southeast Circuit, Grand Commander, and Governor of Jing Province, to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jing Province was then under Eastern Wei control, the people still yearned for the former dynasty. Xin was therefore appointed Grand General of the Guard, Commander of Military Affairs in the Three Jing Provinces, concurrently Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, Commissioner of the Southeast Circuit, Grand Commander, and Governor of Jing Province, to win their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 既至，東魏刺史辛纂出戰，信縱兵擊纂，大敗之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Eastern Wei governor Xin Zuan came out to fight; Xin unleashed his troops and attacked Zuan, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Eastern Wei Governor Xin Zuan came out to give battle. Xin unleashed his troops, attacked Zuan, and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 都督楊忠等前驅斬纂，於是三荊遂定。

translations.literal: The Commander Yang Zhong and others as vanguard beheaded Zuan, and thus the Three Jing were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yang Zhong and others, leading the vanguard, beheaded Zuan, and the Three Jing provinces were thereby secured.

sentences.zh: 東魏又遣其將高敖曹、侯景等奄至。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again sent its generals Gao Aocao, Hou Jing, and others, who suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent its generals Gao Aocao, Hou Jing, and others, who suddenly arrived.

sentences.zh: 信以眾寡不敵，遂率麾下奔梁。

translations.literal: Xin, finding his forces too few to match the enemy, then led his subordinates and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his forces too few to match the enemy, Xin led his followers and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 居三載，梁武帝方許信還北。

translations.literal: After three years, Emperor Wu of Liang finally permitted Xin to return north.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, Emperor Wu of Liang finally permitted Xin to return to the north.

sentences.zh: 信父母既在山東，梁武帝問信所往，答以事君無二。

translations.literal: Since Xin's parents were in Shandong, Emperor Wu of Liang asked where Xin was going; he answered that in serving one's lord there is no second choice.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xin's parents were in Shandong, Emperor Wu of Liang asked where he intended to go. He answered that in serving one's lord there could be no second allegiance.

sentences.zh: 梁武義之，禮送甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang admired this and sent him off with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang admired his loyalty and sent him off with great honor.

sentences.zh: 大統三年至長安，以虧損國威，上書謝罪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he reached Chang'an and, because he had diminished the state's prestige, submitted a memorial asking forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he reached Chang'an and, having diminished the state's prestige, submitted a memorial asking forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝付尚書議之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei entrusted the matter to the Department of State Affairs for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei referred the matter to the Department of State Affairs for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 七兵尚書、陳郡王玄等議，以為既經恩降，請赦罪復職。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince Xuan of Chen Commandery, and others deliberated and held that since he had already been shown imperial grace in being allowed to return, his crime should be pardoned and his office restored.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Seven Armies Prince Xuan of Chen Commandery and others held that, since he had already been shown imperial grace in being permitted to return, his crime should be pardoned and his office restored.

sentences.zh: 詔轉驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府。

translations.literal: An edict transferred him to General of Agile Cavalry, additionally made him Palace Attendant and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred him to General of Agile Cavalry and additionally appointed him Palace Attendant and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋拜領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 仍從復弘農，破沙苑，改封河內郡公。

translations.literal: He then followed in the recapture of Hongnong and the defeat at Shayuan, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He then took part in the recapture of Hongnong and the Battle of Shayuan, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 俘虜中有信親屬，始得父凶問，乃發喪行服。

translations.literal: Among the captives were Xin's relatives, and only then did he receive news of his father's death; he then began mourning and donned mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Among the captives were Xin's relatives, and only then did he receive word of his father's death. He began mourning and donned mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 尋起為大都督，與馮翊王元季海入洛陽，潁、豫、襄、廣、陳留之地並款附。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to serve as Grand Commander and entered Luoyang with Prince Yuan Jihai of Fengyi; the regions of Ying, Yu, Xiang, Guang, and Chenliu all submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as Grand Commander and entered Luoyang with Prince Yuan Jihai of Fengyi. The regions of Ying, Yu, Xiang, Guang, and Chenliu all submitted in good faith.

sentences.zh: 四年，東魏將侯景等圍洛陽，信據金墉城，隨方拒守然有餘日。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Eastern Wei generals Hou Jing and others besieged Luoyang; Xin held Jinyong City and resisted from various directions for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Eastern Wei generals Hou Jing and others besieged Luoyang. Xin held Jinyong City and resisted from every direction for many days.

sentences.zh: 及周文帝至瀍東，景等退走。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou reached the east bank of the Chan River, Jing and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou reached the east bank of the Chan River, Hou Jing and the others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 信與李遠為右軍，戰不處，東魏遂有洛陽。

translations.literal: Xin and Li Yuan were the right wing army; they could not prevail in battle, and Eastern Wei then took Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Li Yuan commanded the right wing, but could not prevail in battle, and Eastern Wei then took Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，侯景寇荊州，周文令信與李弼出武關，景退。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Hou Jing raided Jing Province; Zhou Wen ordered Xin and Li Bi to march out through Wuguan Pass, and Jing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Hou Jing raided Jing Province. Emperor Wen ordered Xin and Li Bi to march out through Wuguan Pass, and Hou Jing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 即以信為大使，尉撫三荊。

translations.literal: Xin was then made Grand Ambassador to comfort and pacify the Three Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Ambassador to comfort and pacify the Three Jing provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋除隴右十一州大都督、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Commander of the Eleven Provinces of Longyou and Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand Commander of the Eleven Provinces of Longyou and Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 先是守宰闇弱，政令乖方，人有冤訟，歷年不能斷決。

translations.literal: Previously the governors and magistrates had been weak and incompetent, government orders had been misapplied, and when people had grievances and lawsuits, cases could not be decided for years.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the governors and magistrates had been weak and incompetent, government orders had been misapplied, and lawsuits could go unresolved for years.

sentences.zh: 及信在州，事無擁滯。

translations.literal: When Xin was in the province, no affairs were blocked or delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xin took office in the province, no affairs were blocked or delayed.

sentences.zh: 示以禮教，勸以耕桑，數年之中，公私富實，流人願附者數萬家。

translations.literal: He displayed ritual teaching and encouraged farming and sericulture; within a few years both public and private stores were rich and full, and tens of thousands of refugee families wished to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed the teachings of ritual and encouraged farming and sericulture. Within a few years both public and private stores were rich and full, and tens of thousands of refugee families wished to settle under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 周文以其信著遐邇，故賜名為信。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen, because his trustworthiness was known near and far, therefore granted him the name Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, because his trustworthiness was known near and far, granted him the name Xin, "Trust."

sentences.zh: 七年，岷州刺史赤水蕃王梁ＧＣ定舉兵反，詔信討之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Liang Ding, king of the Chishui tribes in Min Province, raised troops in rebellion; an edict ordered Xin to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Liang Ding, king of the Chishui tribes in Min Province, raised troops in rebellion, and an edict ordered Xin to suppress him.

sentences.zh: ＧＣ定尋為其部下所殺，而ＧＣ定子弟仍收其餘眾。

translations.literal: Liang Ding was soon killed by his subordinates, but Liang Ding's younger kinsmen still gathered his remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ding was soon killed by his subordinates, but his younger kinsmen still gathered his remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 信乃勒兵向萬年，頓三交穀口。

translations.literal: Xin then led his troops toward Wannian and encamped at the mouth of Sanjiao Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then led his troops toward Wannian and encamped at the mouth of Sanjiao Valley.

sentences.zh: 賊並力拒守。

translations.literal: The bandits combined their strength to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels combined their strength to resist and defend.

sentences.zh: 信因詭道趣稠松嶺。

translations.literal: Xin then took a deceptive route toward Chousong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then took a deceptive route toward Chousong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊不虞信兵之至，望風奔潰。

translations.literal: The bandits did not expect Xin's troops to arrive; at the sight of them they fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not expect Xin's troops to arrive and fled in rout at the sight of them.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，徑至城下，賊並出降。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit, he went straight to the city walls, and the bandits all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory in pursuit, he went straight to the city walls, and the rebels all came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 加授太子太保。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，大軍不利。

translations.literal: In the battle of Mangshan the great army was unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Mangshan the main army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 信與于謹帥散卒自後擊之，齊神武追騎驚擾，國因此得全。

translations.literal: Xin and Yu Jin led scattered soldiers to strike from the rear; Gao Huan's pursuing cavalry were thrown into alarm and confusion, and the state was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Yu Jin led scattered soldiers to strike from the rear. Gao Huan's pursuing cavalry were thrown into alarm and confusion, and the state was thereby preserved.

sentences.zh: 及涼州刺史宇文仲和據州不受代，周文令信率開府怡峰討之。

translations.literal: When Governor of Liang Province Yuwen Zhonghe held the province and refused to accept replacement, Zhou Wen ordered Xin to lead the Director of the Department of State Affairs Yi Feng to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor of Liang Province Yuwen Zhonghe held the province and refused to accept replacement, Emperor Wen ordered Xin to lead Director of the Department of State Affairs Yi Feng to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 仲和嬰城固守，信夜令諸將以沖梯攻其東北，信親率壯士襲其西南，達明克之。

translations.literal: Zhonghe defended the city with his infants; at night Xin ordered the generals to attack the northeast with scaling ladders, while he personally led picked warriors to assault the southwest; at dawn the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe defended the city obstinately. At night Xin ordered his generals to attack the northeast with scaling ladders while he personally led picked warriors to assault the southwest. At dawn the city fell.

sentences.zh: 禽仲和，虜其六千戶送于長安。

translations.literal: He captured Zhonghe and took six thousand households captive, sending them to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Zhonghe and took six thousand households captive, sending them to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 拜大司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 十三年，大軍南討。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the great army marched south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the main army marched south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 時以蠕蠕為寇，令信移鎮河陽。

translations.literal: At that time because the Rouran were raiding, Xin was ordered to transfer his garrison to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Rouran were raiding at that time, Xin was ordered to transfer his garrison to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進位柱國大將軍，錄前後功，增封，聽回授諸子。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was advanced to Pillar of the State and Grand General; his past and present merits were recorded, his fief was increased, and he was permitted to transfer portions to his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Pillar of the State and Grand General. His past and present merits were recorded, his fief was increased, and he was permitted to transfer portions to his sons.

sentences.zh: 於是第二子善，封魏寧縣公；

translations.literal: Thereupon his second son Shan was enfeoffed as Duke of Weining County;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his second son Shan was enfeoffed as Duke of Weining County;

sentences.zh: 第三子穆，必要縣侯；

translations.literal: his third son Mu as Marquis of Biyao County;
translations.idiomatic: his third son Mu as Marquis of Biyao County;

sentences.zh: 第四子藏，義甯縣侯，邑各一千戶。

translations.literal: his fourth son Zang as Marquis of Yining County, each with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: his fourth son Zang as Marquis of Yining County, each with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 第五子順，武成縣侯；

translations.literal: his fifth son Shun as Marquis of Wucheng County;
translations.idiomatic: his fifth son Shun as Marquis of Wucheng County;

sentences.zh: 第六子陀，建忠縣伯，邑各五百戶。

translations.literal: his sixth son Tuo as Viscount of Jianzhong County, each with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: his sixth son Tuo as Viscount of Jianzhong County, each with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 信在隴右歲久，啟求還朝，周文不許。

translations.literal: Xin had long been in Longyou and repeatedly petitioned to return to court, but Zhou Wen did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had long served in Longyou and repeatedly petitioned to return to court, but Emperor Wen would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 或有自東魏來者，又告其母凶問，信發喪行服。

translations.literal: Some who came from Eastern Wei also reported news of his mother's death; Xin began mourning and donned mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Some who came from Eastern Wei also brought word of his mother's death, and Xin began mourning and donned mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 信陳哀苦，請終禮制，又不許。

translations.literal: Xin stated his grief and anguish and requested to complete the full mourning rites, but again was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xin stated his grief and anguish and asked to complete the full mourning rites, but again was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 於是追贈信父庫者司空公，追封信母費連氏常山郡君。

translations.literal: Thereupon his father Kuze was posthumously granted Duke of Works, and his mother Lady Feilian was posthumously granted Lady of Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his father Kuze was posthumously granted Duke of Works, and his mother Lady Feilian was posthumously granted Lady of Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，遷大宗伯，進封衛國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Xin was transferred to Grand Minister of the Ancestors, advanced to Duke of Wei State with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Xin was transferred to Grand Minister of the Ancestors and promoted to Duke of Wei State with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 趙貴誅後，信以同謀坐免。

translations.literal: After Zhao Gui was executed, Xin was dismissed from office for complicity in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Gui was executed, Xin was dismissed from office for complicity in the plot.

sentences.zh: 居無幾，晉公護又欲殺之，以其名望素重，不欲顯其罪過，逼令自盡于家，時年五十五。

translations.literal: Before long, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu again wished to kill him; because his fame and standing had long been great, Hu did not wish to expose his crimes openly and forced him to take his own life at home; he was fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu again wished to kill him. Because his fame and standing had long been great, Hu did not wish to expose his crimes openly and forced him to take his own life at home. He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 信美風度，雅有奇謀大略。

translations.literal: Xin had a fine bearing and elegant manner, and possessed remarkable stratagems and broad plans.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had a fine bearing and elegant manner, and possessed remarkable stratagems and broad plans.

sentences.zh: 周文初啟霸業，唯有關中之地，以隴右形勝，故委信鎮之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen first began his hegemonic enterprise, he had only the lands of Guanzhong; because Longyou was strategically advantageous terrain, he entrusted Xin to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen first began his hegemonic enterprise, he held only the lands of Guanzhong. Because Longyou was strategically vital terrain, he entrusted Xin to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 既為百姓所懷，聲震鄰國。

translations.literal: He was cherished by the common people, and his reputation shook neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: He was cherished by the common people, and his reputation resounded in neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 東魏將侯景之南奔梁也，魏收為檄梁文，矯稱信據隴右，不從宇文氏，乃云「無關西之憂」，欲以委梁人也。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Wei general Hou Jing fled south to Liang, Wei Shou wrote a proclamation to Liang, falsely claiming that Xin held Longyou and would not follow the Yuwen clan, saying there was "no worry about the west of the passes," intending to make the Liang people trust him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Wei general Hou Jing fled south to Liang, Wei Shou wrote a proclamation to Liang falsely claiming that Xin held Longyou and would not follow the Yuwen clan, saying there was "no worry about the lands west of the passes," intending to make the Liang people trust Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 又信在秦州，嘗因獵日暮，馳馬入城，其帽微側，詰旦而吏人有戴帽者，咸慕信而側帽焉。

translations.literal: Also, when Xin was in Qin Province, once while hunting at dusk he galloped into the city with his cap slightly askew; by the next morning all the clerks and commoners who wore caps were imitating Xin and wearing their caps askew.
translations.idiomatic: Also, when Xin was in Qin Province, once while hunting at dusk he galloped into the city with his cap slightly askew. By the next morning all the clerks and commoners who wore caps were imitating him and wearing their caps askew.

sentences.zh: 其為鄰境及士庶所重如此。

translations.literal: This is how greatly he was esteemed by neighboring territories and gentry and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held by neighboring territories and by gentry and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 子羅，先在東魏，乃以次子善為嗣。

translations.literal: His son Luo was previously in Eastern Wei, so his second son Shan was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luo was still in Eastern Wei, so his second son Shan was made heir.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，羅至而善卒，又以羅主嗣。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, Luo arrived but Shan had died, so Luo was again made principal heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was pacified, Luo arrived, but Shan had already died, so Luo was again made principal heir.

sentences.zh: 信長女周明敬後，第四女元貞後，第七女隋文獻後。

translations.literal: Xin's eldest daughter became Empress Mingjing; his fourth daughter became Empress Yuanzhen; his seventh daughter became Empress Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's eldest daughter became Empress Mingjing; his fourth daughter became Empress Yuanzhen; his seventh daughter became Empress Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 周、隋及皇家三代皆為外戚，自古以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: The Zhou, Sui, and imperial houses of three dynasties were all connected by marriage—such a thing had never existed since ancient times.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou, Sui, and imperial houses of three dynasties were all connected by marriage through his daughters—such a thing had never existed since ancient times.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，乃下詔褒贈信太師、上柱國、十州諸軍事、冀州刺史，封趙國公，邑一萬戶，諡曰恭，信母費連氏贈太尉趙恭公夫人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he issued an edict praising and posthumously granting Xin the titles of Grand Preceptor, Pillar of the State, Commander of Military Affairs in Ten Provinces, and Governor of Ji Province, enfeoffing him as Duke of Zhao State with a fief of ten thousand households and the posthumous title Gong; Xin's mother Lady Feilian was posthumously granted Lady of Grand Commandant Duke of Zhao State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he issued an edict praising and posthumously granting Xin the titles of Grand Preceptor, Pillar of the State, Commander of Military Affairs in Ten Provinces, and Governor of Ji Province, enfeoffed him as Duke of Zhao State with a fief of ten thousand households and the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful," and posthumously granted Xin's mother Lady Feilian the title Lady of Grand Commandant Duke of Zhao State.

sentences.zh: 羅，字羅仁。

translations.literal: Luo, courtesy name Luoren.
translations.idiomatic: Luo, courtesy name Luoren.

sentences.zh: 父信隨魏孝武入關中，羅遂為高氏所囚。

translations.literal: When his father Xin followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into Guanzhong, Luo was then taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Xin followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into Guanzhong, Luo was taken prisoner by the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 及信為宇文護誅，羅始見釋。

translations.literal: When Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was finally released.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was finally released.

sentences.zh: 寓居中山，孤貧無以自給。

translations.literal: He lived in Zhongshan, alone and poor, with no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Zhongshan, alone and poor, with no means to support himself.

sentences.zh: 齊將獨孤永業以宗族故，哀之，為買田宅，遺以資畜。

translations.literal: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, out of clan sympathy, took pity on him, bought him fields and a house, and gave him livestock and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, out of clan sympathy, took pity on him, bought him fields and a house, and gave him livestock and supplies.

sentences.zh: 初，信入關後，復娶二妻。

translations.literal: At first, after Xin entered the passes, he took two more wives.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin entered the Guanzhong region, he took two more wives.

sentences.zh: 郭氏生子六人，善、穆、藏、順、陀、整；

translations.literal: Lady Guo bore six sons: Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo bore six sons: Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng;

sentences.zh: 崔氏生隋獻皇后。

translations.literal: Lady Cui bore the Empress Wenxian of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui bore the Empress Wenxian of Sui.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，隋文帝為定州總管，獻皇后遣人求羅，得之。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wen of Sui was Area Commander of Ding Province; Empress Wenxian sent people to seek out Luo and found him.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, Emperor Wen of Sui was Area Commander of Ding Province. Empress Wenxian sent people to seek out Luo and found him.

sentences.zh: 相見悲不自勝，侍御者皆泣。

translations.literal: When they met, their grief was beyond bearing, and all those in attendance wept.
translations.idiomatic: When they met, their grief was beyond bearing, and all those in attendance wept.

sentences.zh: 於是厚遺車馬財物。

translations.literal: Thereupon he generously bestowed carriages, horses, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then gave him a generous gift of carriages, horses, and other valuables.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周武帝以羅功臣子，久淪異域，徵拜楚安郡太守。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Wu of Zhou, because Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long lost in foreign lands, summoned and appointed him Governor of Chu'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Wu of Zhou, noting that Luo was the son of a meritorious minister who had long languished in foreign territory, summoned him and appointed him Governor of Chu'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以疾去官，歸京師。

translations.literal: Because of illness he resigned his office and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his office due to illness and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸弟見羅少長貧賤，每輕侮，不以兄禮事之。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, seeing that Luo had grown up in poverty and low station, often treated him lightly and disrespectfully and did not serve him with the rites due an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers, knowing he had grown up in poverty and low station, often treated him with contempt and did not show him the respect due an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 然性長者，亦不與諸弟校競長短。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was a man of forbearance and did not compete with his younger brothers over who was right or wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was forbearing and did not quarrel with his younger brothers over petty slights.

sentences.zh: 後由是重之。

translations.literal: Afterward they therefore respected him.
translations.idiomatic: After that they came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 文帝為丞相，拜羅儀同，常置左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, Luo was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs and was constantly kept at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, he appointed Luo Director of the Department of State Affairs and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，詔追贈羅父。

translations.literal: After receiving the abdication, an edict posthumously granted titles to Luo's father.
translations.idiomatic: After founding the dynasty, the emperor issued an edict posthumously honoring Luo's father.

sentences.zh: 其諸弟以羅母沒齊，先無夫人號，不當承襲。

translations.literal: His younger brothers argued that because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never held the title of Lady, he should not inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers argued that because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never held the title of Lady, he was not entitled to inherit the ducal line.

sentences.zh: 上以問後，後曰：「羅誠嫡長，不可誣也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the empress, who said: "Luo is truly the legitimate eldest son; this cannot be falsified."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the empress, who replied, "Luo is truly the legitimate eldest son. That cannot be denied.

sentences.zh: 於是襲爵趙國公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he inherited the title of Duke of Zhao State.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he inherited the title of Duke of Zhao State.

sentences.zh: 以其弟善為河內郡公，穆為金泉縣公，藏為武平縣公，陀為武喜縣公，整為千牛備身。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shan was made Duke of Henei Commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan County, Zang Duke of Wuping County, Tuo Duke of Wuxi County, and Zheng a Guard of the Thousand-Ox Guard of the Body.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shan was made Duke of Henei Commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan County, Zang Duke of Wuping County, Tuo Duke of Wuxi County, and Zheng a Guard of the Thousand-Ox Guard of the Body.

sentences.zh: 擢拜羅為左領左右將軍，遷左衛將軍，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Luo was promoted and appointed General of the Left Guard of the Left and Right, then transferred to General of the Left Guard; rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was promoted to General of the Left Guard of the Left and Right, then transferred to General of the Left Guard. The rewards he received before and after were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 出為涼州總管，進位上柱國，徵拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Area Commander of Liang Province, was advanced to Pillar of the State, and was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Left Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Area Commander of Liang Province, promoted to Pillar of the State, and then summoned to serve as Grand General of the Left Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，改封蜀國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shu State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shu State.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒官，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office and was given the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 子纂嗣，位河陽都尉。

translations.literal: His son Zuan succeeded and held the position of Commandant of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan succeeded to the line and served as Commandant of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 纂弟武都，大業末，亦為河陽都尉。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Wudu, at the end of Daye, also served as Commandant of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Wudu also served as Commandant of Heyang at the end of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 庶長子開遠。

translations.literal: The eldest son by a concubine was Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son by a concubine was Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，裴虔通率賊入成象殿，宿衛兵士皆從逆。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, Pei Qiantong led the rebels into Chengxian Hall, and the palace guard soldiers all joined the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Pei Qiantong led the rebels into Chengxian Hall, and the palace guard soldiers all joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 開遠時為千牛，與獨孤盛力戰合下，為賊所執，賊義而舍之。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan was then in the Thousand-Ox Guard; together with Dugu Sheng he fought fiercely below the hall platform, was seized by the rebels, and the rebels admired his courage and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan was then in the Thousand-Ox Guard. He and Dugu Sheng fought fiercely on the steps below the hall, were seized by the rebels, and the rebels, admiring their courage, released them.

sentences.zh: 善字伏陀。

translations.literal: Shan, courtesy name Futo.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, courtesy name Futo.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，善騎射，以父勳，封魏寧縣公。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and skilled in horsemanship and archery; because of his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weining County.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood and skilled in horsemanship and archery, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weining County on account of his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，又以父勳，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵長城郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, again because of his father's merit he was granted General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, additionally made Palace Attendant, and advanced to Duke of Changcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, again on account of his father's merit he was granted General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, additionally appointed Palace Attendant, and promoted to Duke of Changcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，除河州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was appointed Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was appointed Governor of He Province.

sentences.zh: 以父負釁，久廢於家。

translations.literal: Because his father bore guilt, he was long kept idle at home.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had been implicated in guilt, he was kept idle at home for a long time.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，乃授龍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was then appointed Governor of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding he was appointed Governor of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，襲爵河內郡公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he inherited the title of Duke of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he inherited the title of Duke of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從帝東討，以功授上開府。

translations.literal: Following the emperor on the eastern campaign, for his merit he was granted Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern campaign he followed the emperor and, for his merit, was granted Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋除兗州刺史，政在簡惠，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yan Province; his government was simple and benevolent, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Governor of Yan Province. His government was simple and benevolent, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，贈持節、柱國、五州諸軍事、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in the province and was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Pillar of the State, Commander of Military Affairs in Five Provinces, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted the titles of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Pillar of the State, Commander of Military Affairs in Five Provinces, and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子覽嗣，位右候衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Lan succeeded and held the position of Grand General of the Right Guard of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan succeeded to the line and served as Grand General of the Right Guard of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 大業末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the end of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 陀字黎邪。

translations.literal: Tuo, courtesy name Lixie.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo, courtesy name Lixie.

sentences.zh: 仕周，胥附上士。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he was a Senior Attendant of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as Senior Attendant of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 坐父徙蜀十餘年，宇文護誅，始歸長安。

translations.literal: Because of his father he was exiled to Shu for more than ten years; after Yuwen Hu was executed, he finally returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's guilt he was exiled to Shu for more than ten years. After Yuwen Hu was executed, he finally returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝禪，拜上開府、領左右將軍，累轉延州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Tuo was appointed Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs and General of the Left and Right Guards, and was repeatedly transferred until he became Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui founded the dynasty, Tuo was appointed Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs and General of the Left and Right Guards, and later served as Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 陀性好左道，其外祖母高氏先事貓鬼，已殺其舅郭沙羅，因轉入其家。

translations.literal: Tuo by nature favored heterodox ways; his maternal grandmother Lady Gao had first served the cat ghost, had already killed his maternal uncle Guo Shaluo, and the practice then passed into his household.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo by nature favored heterodox practices. His maternal grandmother Lady Gao had first served the cat ghost, had already used it to kill his maternal uncle Guo Shaluo, and the practice then passed into his household.

sentences.zh: 上微聞而不信。

translations.literal: The emperor heard faint rumors but did not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard faint rumors but did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 會獻皇后及楊素妻鄭氏俱有疾，召醫視之，皆曰：「此貓鬼疾。」

translations.literal: It happened that Empress Wenxian and Yang Su's wife Lady Zheng were both ill; physicians were summoned to examine them, and all said: "This is cat-ghost sickness."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenxian and Yang Su's wife Lady Zheng both fell ill, physicians were summoned and all declared, "This is cat-ghost sickness.

sentences.zh: 上以陀，後之異母弟，陀妻，楊素之異母妹，由是意陀所為。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, and therefore suspected Tuo's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and that Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, and therefore suspected Tuo.

sentences.zh: 陰令其兄左監門郎將穆以情喻之，上又避左右諷陀，陀言無有。

translations.literal: Secretly he had Tuo's elder brother Mu, Colonel of the Left Gate Guard, explain the matter to him with feeling; the emperor also, avoiding those nearby, hinted to Tuo, but Tuo said there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he had Tuo's elder brother Mu, Colonel of the Left Gate Guard, reason with him privately. The emperor also hinted to Tuo when no one else was present, but Tuo denied everything.

sentences.zh: 上不說，左轉遷州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and transferred him to the left as Governor of Qian Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and demoted him to Governor of Qian Province.

sentences.zh: 出怨言，上令左僕射高熲、納言蘇威、大理正皇甫孝緒、大理丞楊遠等雜案之。

translations.literal: He uttered resentful words; the emperor ordered Vice Director of the Left Gao Jiong, Chief Counselor Su Wei, Chief Judge of the Court of Justice Huangfu Xiaoxu, Assistant Judge of the Court of Justice Yang Yuan, and others jointly to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: He uttered resentful words, and the emperor ordered Vice Director of the Left Gao Jiong, Chief Counselor Su Wei, Chief Judge Huangfu Xiaoxu, Assistant Judge Yang Yuan, and others to investigate the case jointly.

sentences.zh: 陀婢徐阿尼言：本從陀母家來，常事貓鬼，每以子日夜祀之。

translations.literal: Tuo's maid Xu Ani said: she had originally come from Tuo's mother's household, constantly served the cat ghost, and every night sacrificed to it with rats.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had originally come from Tuo's mother's household, had constantly served the cat ghost, and every night sacrificed rats to it.

sentences.zh: 言子者鼠也。

translations.literal: By "children" she meant rats.
translations.idiomatic: By "children" she meant rats.

sentences.zh: 其貓鬼每殺人者，所死家財物潛移於畜貓鬼家。

translations.literal: Whenever the cat ghost killed someone, the wealth and goods of the dead person's household were secretly transferred to the household that kept the cat ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the cat ghost killed someone, the wealth of the dead person's household was secretly transferred to the household that kept the cat ghost.

sentences.zh: 陀嘗從家中索酒，其妻曰：「無錢可酤。」

translations.literal: Tuo once asked for wine at home; his wife said: "There is no money to buy any."
