translations.idiomatic: Tuo once asked for wine at home. His wife said, "There is no money to buy any.

sentences.zh: 陀因謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向越公家，使我足錢。」

translations.literal: Tuo then said to Ani: "You can send the cat ghost to the Duke of Yue's household and make me have enough money."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo then told Ani, "Send the cat ghost to the Duke of Yue's household and get me enough money."

sentences.zh: 阿尼便咒之，居數日，貓鬼向素家。

translations.literal: Ani then cast spells, and within a few days the cat ghost went to Su's household.
translations.idiomatic: Ani cast the spell, and within a few days the cat ghost went to Yang Su's household.

sentences.zh: 後上初從并州還，陀於園中謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向皇后所，使多賜吾物。」

translations.literal: Later when the emperor had just returned from Bing Province, Tuo said to Ani in the garden: "You can send the cat ghost to the empress's quarters and make her bestow many things on me."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor had just returned from Bing Province, Tuo told Ani in the garden, "Send the cat ghost to the empress's quarters and make her bestow many gifts on me.

sentences.zh: 阿尼復咒之，遂入宮中。

translations.literal: Ani again cast spells, and it then entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ani cast the spell again, and the cat ghost entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 楊遠乃于門下外省遣阿尼呼貓鬼，阿尼於是夜中置香粥一盆，以匙扣而呼曰：「貓女可來，無住宮中。」

translations.literal: Yang Yuan then sent Ani from the Outer Secretariat of the Gate Department to summon the cat ghost; Ani placed a bowl of fragrant porridge at night, tapped it with a spoon, and called out: "Cat girl, you may come; do not stay in the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuan then had Ani summoned from the Outer Secretariat to call the cat ghost. That night Ani placed a bowl of fragrant porridge, tapped it with a spoon, and called out, "Cat girl, you may come—do not remain in the palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，阿尼色正青，若被牽拽者，雲貓鬼已到。

translations.literal: After a long while Ani's face turned blue-green, as if being pulled and dragged, and she said the cat ghost had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Ani's face turned blue-green, as if she were being pulled and dragged, and she declared that the cat ghost had arrived.

sentences.zh: 上以其事下公卿。

translations.literal: The emperor submitted the matter to the high officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the matter to the high officials.

sentences.zh: 奇章公牛弘曰：「妖由人興，殺其人，可以絕矣。」

translations.literal: Niu Hong of Qizhang said: "Evil spirits arise through men; kill the man and it can be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong of Qizhang said, "Evil arises through men. Kill the man and the evil can be ended.

sentences.zh: 上令犢車載陀夫妻，將賜死於其家。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an ox cart to carry Tuo and his wife and was about to grant them death at their home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an ox cart to carry Tuo and his wife home, where they were to be granted death.

sentences.zh: 陀弟司勳侍中整詣闕求哀，於是免陀死，除名，以其妻楊氏為尼。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng, Palace Attendant in the Ministry of Merit, went to the palace gate to beg for mercy; thereupon Tuo's death was remitted, his name was struck from the rolls, and his wife Lady Yang was made a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's younger brother Zheng, Palace Attendant in the Ministry of Merit, went to the palace gate to beg for mercy. Tuo was spared death but struck from the rolls, and his wife Lady Yang was made a nun.

sentences.zh: 先是有人訟其母為人貓鬼所殺者，上以為妖妄，怒而遣之。

translations.literal: Previously someone had sued, claiming his mother was killed by another's cat ghost; the emperor considered this superstitious nonsense, grew angry, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Previously someone had sued, claiming his mother was killed by another person's cat ghost. The emperor considered this superstitious nonsense, grew angry, and dismissed the case.

sentences.zh: 及此，詔誅被訟行貓鬼家。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered the execution of the household accused of keeping the cat ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the execution of the household accused of keeping the cat ghost.

sentences.zh: 陀未幾而卒，

translations.literal: Tuo died before long,
translations.idiomatic: Tuo died before long,

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，追念舅氏，聽以禮葬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, remembering his maternal uncle, he permitted a burial according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, remembering his maternal uncle, he permitted a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔贈正義大夫。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued posthumously granting him Grand Master of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued posthumously granting him the title Grand Master of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 帝意猶不已，復贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor's feelings were still not satisfied, and he additionally granted him Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's feelings were still not satisfied, and he additionally granted him the title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 二子，延福、延壽。

translations.literal: Two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 陀弟整，位幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng held the position of Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's younger brother Zheng served as Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 大業初，贈金紫光祿大夫、平鄉侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Gold Seal and Marquis of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Gold Seal and Marquis of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 竇熾，字光成，扶風平陵人，後漢大鴻臚章之後也。

translations.literal: Dou Chi, courtesy name Guangcheng, was a man of Pingling in Fufeng, a descendant of Zhang, Grand Minister of State of Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chi, courtesy name Guangcheng, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng and a descendant of Zhang, Grand Minister of State under Later Han.

sentences.zh: 章子統，靈帝時為雁門太守，避竇武之難，亡奔匈奴，遂為部落大人。

translations.literal: Zhang's son Zitong, in the time of Emperor Ling served as Governor of Yanmen; avoiding the disaster of Dou Wu, he fled to the Xiongnu and became a tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's son Zitong served as Governor of Yanmen under Emperor Ling. Fleeing the disaster of Dou Wu, he took refuge with the Xiongnu and became a tribal chieftain.

sentences.zh: 後魏南徙，子孫因家代，賜姓紇豆陵氏。

translations.literal: When Later Wei moved south, his descendants made their home in Dai and were granted the surname Gedouling.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei moved south, his descendants settled in Dai and were granted the surname Gedouling.

sentences.zh: 累世仕魏，皆至大官。

translations.literal: For generations they served Wei and all reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they served Wei and all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 父略，平遠將軍，以熾著勳，贈少保、住國大將軍、建昌公。

translations.literal: His father Lue was General of Pacifying the Distance; because of Chi's outstanding merit he was posthumously granted Junior Tutor, Pillar of the State Grand General, and Duke of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lue was General of Pacifying the Distance. Because of Chi's outstanding merit he was posthumously granted Junior Tutor, Pillar of the State Grand General, and Duke of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 熾性嚴明，有謀略，美須髯，身長八尺二寸。

translations.literal: Chi was by nature stern and clear-minded, possessed stratagems, had a fine beard, and stood eight feet two inches tall.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was stern and clear-minded by nature, possessed of stratagems, handsome of beard, and stood eight feet two inches tall.

sentences.zh: 少從范陽祁忻受《毛詩》、《左氏春秋》，略通大義。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Mao Odes and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals under Qi Xin of Fanyang and gained a general understanding of their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Mao Odes and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals under Qi Xin of Fanyang and gained a general understanding of their meaning.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and his physical strength surpassed that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，北鎮擾亂，乃隨略避地定州，投葛榮。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang in Wei, when the northern garrisons were in turmoil, he followed Lue to take refuge in Ding Province and joined Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, when the northern garrisons were in turmoil, he followed his father Lue to take refuge in Ding Province and joined Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮欲官略，略不受。

translations.literal: Rong wished to give Lue an office, but Lue would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong wished to give Lue an office, but Lue refused.

sentences.zh: 榮疑其有異志，遂留略于冀州，將熾及熾兄善隨軍。

translations.literal: Rong suspected he had a different intent and therefore kept Lue in Ji Province while taking Chi and Chi's elder brother Shan with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong suspected he harbored a different allegiance and therefore kept Lue in Ji Province while taking Chi and Chi's elder brother Shan with the army.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮破葛榮，熾乃將家隨榮於并州。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong defeated Ge Rong, Chi then brought his family and followed Rong to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong defeated Ge Rong, Chi brought his family and followed Rong to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮別帥韓婁等據薊城不下，以熾為都督，從驃騎將軍侯深討之。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong's separate commander Han Lou and others held Ji City and would not submit; Chi was made Commander and followed General of Agile Cavalry Hou Shen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ge Rong's subordinate commander Han Lou and others held Ji City and would not submit. Chi was made Commander and followed General of Agile Cavalry Hou Shen to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 熾手斬婁，以功拜揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: Chi personally beheaded Lou and for his merit was appointed General Who Displays Fury.
translations.idiomatic: Chi personally beheaded Han Lou and, for his merit, was appointed General Who Displays Fury.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，別封真定縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Zhending County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Zhending County.

sentences.zh: 從周文帝禽竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wen of Zhou he captured Dou Tai, recaptured Hongnong, and defeated Shayuan, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wen of Zhou he helped capture Dou Tai, recapture Hongnong, and win at Shayuan, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，諸將退走，熾時獨從兩騎，為敵人追至芒山。

translations.literal: In the battle of Heqiao the generals retreated and fled; Chi at that time was alone with two horsemen and was pursued by the enemy to Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heqiao the generals retreated, and Chi was left alone with two horsemen, pursued by the enemy all the way to Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 熾乃下馬，背山抗之。

translations.literal: Chi then dismounted, backed against the mountain, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Chi dismounted, backed against the mountain, and made his stand.

sentences.zh: 俄而敵眾漸多，矢下如雨，熾騎士所執弓，並為敵人所射破。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy grew steadily more numerous, arrows fell like rain, and the bows held by Chi's horsemen were all shot through by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy grew steadily more numerous, arrows fell like rain, and the bows held by Chi's horsemen were all shot through by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 熾乃總收其箭以射之，所中人馬，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Chi then gathered all the arrows and shot them back; every man and horse he hit fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Chi then gathered the fallen arrows and shot them back. Every man and horse he hit fell at the twang of the bowstring.

sentences.zh: 敵乃相謂曰：「得此三人，未足為功。」

translations.literal: The enemy then said to one another: "To capture these three men would not be worth the effort."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then said to one another, "To capture these three men would not be worth the effort.

sentences.zh: 乃稍引退。

translations.literal: They then gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They then gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 熾因其怠，遂突圍得出。

translations.literal: Chi, taking advantage of their slackness, then broke through the encirclement and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of their slackness, Chi broke through the encirclement and escaped.

sentences.zh: 又從太保李弼討白額稽胡，破之。

translations.literal: He again followed Grand Tutor Li Bi to suppress the White-Forehead Jiehu and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand Tutor Li Bi to suppress the White-Forehead Jiehu and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫州來，熾從周文援之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi came over with Northern Yu Province, Chi followed Zhou Wen to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi defected with Northern Yu Province, Chi followed Emperor Wen to aid him.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，會東魏人據芒山為陣，周文命留輜于瀍曲，率輕騎奮擊，中軍與右軍大破之，悉虜其步卒。

translations.literal: When they reached Luoyang, it happened that Eastern Wei men held Mangshan in battle formation; Zhou Wen ordered the baggage left at Chan Bend, led light cavalry in a fierce attack, and the center and right armies inflicted a great defeat and captured all their infantry.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Luoyang, Eastern Wei forces had taken up a battle formation on Mangshan. Emperor Wen left the baggage at Chan Bend, led light cavalry in a fierce attack, and the center and right armies inflicted a crushing defeat and captured all their infantry.

sentences.zh: 熾獨追至石濟而還。

translations.literal: Chi alone pursued as far as Shiji and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chi alone pursued as far as Shiji and then returned.

sentences.zh: 大統十三年，進使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Datong he was advanced to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, and additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Datong he was promoted to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and additionally appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為涇州刺史，蒞職數年，政號清靜。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Jing Province; during several years in office his government was called pure and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Governor of Jing Province, and during several years in office his government was renowned for its purity and tranquility.

sentences.zh: 改封安武縣公。

translations.literal: He was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anwu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anwu County.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，除原州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was appointed Governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was appointed Governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 熾抑挫豪右，申理幽滯，在州十載，甚有政績。

translations.literal: Chi restrained the powerful and great families, cleared up hidden and delayed cases, and during ten years in the province achieved very great administrative merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chi restrained the powerful gentry, cleared up long-delayed cases, and during ten years in the province achieved outstanding administrative results.

sentences.zh: 州城北有泉水，熾屢經遊踐，嘗與僚吏宴於泉側，因酌水自飲，曰：「吾在此州，唯當飲水而已。」

translations.literal: North of the provincial city there was a spring; Chi often passed by and visited it, once feasting with his staff officers beside the spring, and as he poured water and drank himself said: "In this province I should drink only water."
translations.idiomatic: North of the provincial city there was a spring that Chi often visited. Once, feasting with his staff beside the spring, he poured water and drank, saying, "In this province I should drink only water.

sentences.zh: 及去職後，人吏感其遺惠，每至此泉者，莫不懷之。

translations.literal: After he left office, officials and commoners, moved by his lingering kindness, whenever they came to this spring could not fail to remember him.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office, officials and commoners, moved by his lingering kindness, never failed to remember him whenever they came to this spring.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，進爵廣武郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong, he was advanced to Duke of Guangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong he was promoted to Duke of Guangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 屬蠕蠕寇廣武，熾與柱國趙貴分路討之。

translations.literal: When the Rouran raided Guangwu, Chi and the Pillar of the State Zhao Gui took separate routes to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided Guangwu, Chi and Zhao Gui, Pillar of the State, took separate routes to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕引退，熾度河至麹伏川追及，大破之。

translations.literal: The Rouran withdrew; Chi crossed the river and pursued them to Qufu River, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran withdrew. Chi crossed the river, pursued them to Qufu River, and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，拜柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng he was appointed Pillar of the State and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng he was appointed Pillar of the State and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 周明帝以熾前朝舊臣，勳望兼重，欲獨為造第。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Zhou, because Chi was an old minister of the former dynasty with combined merit and renown, wished to build a residence for him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Zhou, because Chi was an old minister of the former dynasty whose merit and renown were both great, wished to build a residence for him alone.

sentences.zh: 熾辭以天下未平，干戈未偃，不宜輒發徒役，周明不許。

translations.literal: Chi declined on the grounds that the realm was not yet pacified and weapons had not yet been laid aside, and that it was inappropriate to mobilize laborers; Emperor Ming did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chi declined, saying the realm was not yet pacified and arms had not yet been laid aside, and that it was inappropriate to mobilize laborers. Emperor Ming did not agree.

sentences.zh: 尋而帝崩，事方得寢。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor died and the matter was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died and the matter was finally dropped.

sentences.zh: 熾既朝之元老，名望素隆，至於軍國大謀，常與參議。

translations.literal: Chi was an elder statesman of the court whose renown had long been exalted; as for great plans of state and army, he was constantly consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was an elder statesman of the court whose renown had long been exalted, and he was constantly consulted on great plans of state and army.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，周武帝幸其第問之，因賜金石之樂。

translations.literal: Once when he was ill, Emperor Wu of Zhou visited his residence to inquire after him and granted him bell and stone music.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he fell ill, Emperor Wu of Zhou visited his residence to inquire after him and granted him bell and stone music.

sentences.zh: 其見禮如此。

translations.literal: This is how he was honored.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 帝於大德殿將謀伐齊，熾年已衰老，乃扼腕曰：「臣雖朽邁，請執幹櫓，首啟戎行。

translations.literal: When the emperor at Dade Hall was planning to campaign against Qi, Chi, already old and frail, clenched his wrist and said: "Though I am decayed and aged, I ask to take up shield and oar and lead the army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor at Dade Hall was planning to campaign against Qi, Chi, already old and frail, clenched his wrist and said, "Though I am decayed and aged, I ask to take up shield and spear and lead the army on campaign.

sentences.zh: 得一睹誅翦鯨鯢，廓清寰宇，省方觀俗，登嶽告成，然後歸魂泉壤，無復餘恨。」

translations.literal: To see once the execution of great evils, the clearing of the realm, inspection of the regions and observation of customs, ascent of the sacred peak and announcement of completion, and then return my soul to the grave with no remaining regret."
translations.idiomatic: To see once the destruction of great evils, the clearing of the realm, inspection of the regions and observation of customs, ascent of the sacred peak and announcement of completion, and then return my soul to the grave with no remaining regret.

sentences.zh: 帝壯其志節，遂以熾第二子武當公恭為左二軍總管。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his resolve and therefore made Chi's second son Gong, Duke of Wudang, Commander of the Left Second Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his resolve and therefore made Chi's second son Gong, Duke of Wudang, Commander of the Left Second Army.

sentences.zh: 齊平之後，帝乃召熾曆觀相州宮殿。

translations.literal: After Qi was pacified, the emperor summoned Chi to tour the palaces of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi was pacified, the emperor summoned Chi to tour the palaces of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 熾拜賀曰：「陛下真不負先帝矣。」

translations.literal: Chi bowed in congratulation and said: "Your Majesty has truly not failed the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Chi bowed in congratulation and said, "Your Majesty has truly not failed the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and advanced him to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted him to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，兼雍州牧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he additionally served as Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he additionally served as Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 及周宣營建東京，以熾為京洛營作大監，宮苑制度，皆取決焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan of Zhou built the Eastern Capital, Chi was made Grand Supervisor of Capital and Luoyang Construction; the regulations for palaces and gardens were all decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Zhou built the Eastern Capital, Chi was made Grand Supervisor of Capital and Luoyang Construction, and the regulations for palaces and gardens were all decided by him.

sentences.zh: 大象初，改食樂陵縣，邑戶如舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang his fief income was changed to Leling County with households as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang his fief income was changed to Leling County with the same number of households as before.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝入輔政，停洛陽宮作，熾請入朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui entered to assist in government, construction of the Luoyang palace was halted and Chi requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui entered to assist in government, construction of the Luoyang palace was halted and Chi requested to enter court.

sentences.zh: 屬尉遲迥舉兵，熾乃移入金墉，與洛州刺史、平涼西元亨同心固守，仍權行洛陽鎮事。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Tong raised troops, Chi moved into Jinyong and, together with Governor of Luo Province Yuan Heng of Pingliang West, defended with united hearts, temporarily administering Luoyang garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Tong raised troops, Chi moved into Jinyong and, together with Governor of Luo Province Yuan Heng of Pingliang West, defended with united resolve, temporarily administering Luoyang garrison affairs.

sentences.zh: 相州平，熾方入朝。

translations.literal: When Xiang Province was pacified, Chi finally entered court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Province was pacified, Chi finally entered court.

sentences.zh: 屬文帝初為相國，百僚皆勸進，自以累世受恩，遂不肯署箋，時人綿高其節。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen had just become Chancellor, all the hundred officials urged him to ascend; Chi, considering himself to have received grace across generations, therefore refused to sign the memorial, and people of the time highly praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen had just become Chancellor, all the officials urged him to ascend the throne. Chi, considering that his family had received grace across generations, refused to sign the memorial, and people of the time highly praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐極，拜太傅，加殊禮，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Chi was appointed Grand Tutor with special honors; in audience he was not called by name.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Chi was appointed Grand Tutor with special honors and was not called by name in audience.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年八月薨，時年七十八。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Kaihuang he died at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Kaihuang he died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈八州諸軍事、冀州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Commander of Military Affairs in Eight Provinces and Governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Commander of Military Affairs in Eight Provinces and Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 熾事親孝，奉諸兄以悌順聞。

translations.literal: Chi was filial toward his parents and was known for deferential obedience to his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was filial toward his parents and was known for deferential obedience to his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 及其望位隆重，而子孫皆處列位，遂為當時盛族。

translations.literal: When his rank and standing became exalted and his descendants all held prominent positions, his family became one of the great clans of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When his rank and standing became exalted and his descendants all held prominent positions, his family became one of the great clans of the age.

sentences.zh: 子茂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 茂有弟十三人，恭、威最知名。

translations.literal: Mao had thirteen younger brothers; Gong and Wei were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Mao had thirteen younger brothers; Gong and Wei were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 恭位至大將軍。

translations.literal: Gong rose to the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Gong rose to the rank of Grand General.

sentences.zh: 從周武平齊，封贊國公，除西兗州總管，以罪賜死。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu of Zhou in the pacification of Qi, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zan State, appointed Area Commander of Western Yan Province, and granted death for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu of Zhou in the pacification of Qi, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zan State and appointed Area Commander of Western Yan Province, then granted death for his crime.

sentences.zh: 熾兄善，以中軍大都督、南城公從魏孝武西遷，仕至太僕、衛尉卿、汾北華瀛三州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、永富縣公，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Chi's elder brother Shan, as Grand Commander of the Central Army and Duke of Nancheng, followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west; he served until Grand Coachman, Minister of the Guard, Governor of the Three Provinces of Fenbei, Hua, and Ying, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, Duke of Yongfu County; posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's elder brother Shan, as Grand Commander of the Central Army and Duke of Nancheng, followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west. He served as Grand Coachman, Minister of the Guard, Governor of the Three Provinces of Fenbei, Hua, and Ying, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Duke of Yongfu County, with the posthumous name Zhong, "Loyal."

sentences.zh: 子榮定嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rongding succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongding succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 榮定沉深有器局，容貌魁偉，美須髯，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Rongding was deep and steady with breadth of vision; his appearance was imposing, his beard handsome, and he was skilled in bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding was deep and steady with breadth of vision. He was imposing in appearance, handsome of beard, and skilled in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 初為魏文帝千牛備身，周文帝見而奇之，授平東將軍，賜爵宜君縣子。

translations.literal: At first he served as a Guard of the Thousand-Ox Guard of the Body for Emperor Wen of Wei; Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and was impressed, appointing him General of Pacifying the East and enfeoffing him as Viscount of Yijun County.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a Guard of the Thousand-Ox Guard of the Body for Emperor Wen of Wei. Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and was impressed, appointing him General of Pacifying the East and enfeoffing him as Viscount of Yijun County.

sentences.zh: 後從周文與齊人戰於北芒，周師不利，榮定與汝南公宇文神慶帥精騎擊卻齊師。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zhou Wen in battle against Qi at Beimang; the Zhou army was unsuccessful, but Rongding together with Duke of Runan Yuwen Shenqing led picked cavalry and drove back the Qi army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Wen in battle against Qi at Beimang. The Zhou army was unsuccessful, but Rongding together with Yuwen Shenqing, Duke of Runan, led picked cavalry and drove back the Qi army.

sentences.zh: 以功拜上儀同。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋復以軍功進位開府。

translations.literal: Soon he was again advanced in rank for military merit to Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again for military merit to Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 襲爵永富縣公，除忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title of Duke of Yongfu County and was appointed Governor of Zhong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title of Duke of Yongfu County and was appointed Governor of Zhong Province.

sentences.zh: 從平齊，加上開府，拜前將軍、佽飛中大夫。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Qi, he was additionally granted Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs and appointed Forward General and Grand Master of the Flying Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Following the pacification of Qi, he was additionally granted Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs and appointed Forward General and Grand Master of the Flying Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 其妻，則隋文帝長姊安成長公主也，文帝少與之情契甚厚。

translations.literal: His wife was the elder sister of Emperor Wen of Sui, Princess Anchang; the emperor from youth had been deeply close to her.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the elder sister of Emperor Wen of Sui, Princess Anchang, with whom the emperor had been deeply close from youth.

sentences.zh: 榮定亦知帝有人君之表，尤相推結。

translations.literal: Rongding also knew the emperor bore the countenance of a ruler and especially formed a bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding also recognized that the emperor bore the countenance of a ruler and formed an especially close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 及帝作相，領左右宮伯，使鎮守天臺，總統露門內兩廂仗衛，常宿禁中。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Chancellor, Rongding served as Palace Attendant of the Left and Right and was sent to garrison Tiantai, commanding the guard of the two wings of the Lumen Gate within the palace, regularly staying in the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became Chancellor, Rongding served as Palace Attendant of the Left and Right and was sent to garrison Tiantai, commanding the guard of the two wings of the Lumen Gate within the palace and regularly staying in the forbidden quarters.

sentences.zh: 遇尉遲迥初平，朝廷頗以山東為意，拜榮定為洛州總管以鎮之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Tong had just been pacified, the court was much concerned about Shandong and appointed Rongding Area Commander of Luo Province to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Tong had just been pacified, the court was much concerned about Shandong and appointed Rongding Area Commander of Luo Province to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 前後賜縑四千匹、西涼女樂一部。

translations.literal: Before and after he was granted four thousand bolts of silk and a set of Western Liang female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he was granted four thousand bolts of silk and a set of Western Liang female musicians.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，來朝，賜馬三百匹、部曲八十戶遣之。

translations.literal: When the abdication was received, he came to court and was granted three hundred horses and eighty households of retainers before being sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was founded, he came to court and was granted three hundred horses and eighty households of retainers before being sent back.

sentences.zh: 坐事除名。

translations.literal: For an offense his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense his name was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「天子姊乃作田舍兒妻！」

translations.literal: The princess said: "The emperor's elder sister to become the wife of a peasant!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "The emperor's elder sister reduced to a peasant's wife!

sentences.zh: 上不得已，尋拜右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; soon Rongding was appointed Grand General of the Right Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice. Soon Rongding was appointed Grand General of the Right Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 上數幸其第，恩錫甚厚，每令尚食局日供羊一口，珍味稱是。

translations.literal: The emperor frequently visited his residence and bestowed favor very generously, ordering the Imperial Kitchen daily to supply one sheep and delicacies in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frequently visited his residence and bestowed favor very generously, ordering the Imperial Kitchen daily to supply one sheep and delicacies in proportion.

sentences.zh: 以佐命功，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: For his merit in assisting the founding of the dynasty, he was appointed Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in assisting the founding of the dynasty, he was appointed Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 歷位甯州刺史、右武候大將軍、秦州總管，賜吳樂一部。

translations.literal: He successively held the positions of Governor of Ning Province, Grand General of the Right Military Guard, and Area Commander of Qin Province, and was granted a set of Wu music.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Governor of Ning Province, Grand General of the Right Military Guard, and Area Commander of Qin Province, and was granted a set of Wu music.

sentences.zh: 突厥沙缽略寇邊，為行軍元帥，率總管出涼州。

translations.literal: When the Turkic ruler Shaboluo raided the frontier, Rongding served as Campaign Commander and led area commanders out from Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turkic ruler Shaboluo raided the frontier, Rongding served as Campaign Commander and led area commanders out from Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 與虜戰于高越原，兩軍相持，地無水，士卒渴甚，至刺馬血而飲，死者十二三。

translations.literal: He fought the barbarians at Gaoyue Plain; the two armies faced each other, there was no water in the land, and the soldiers were extremely thirsty, even stabbing their horses to drink the blood; one or two in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the barbarians at Gaoyue Plain. The two armies faced each other where there was no water, and the soldiers were so thirsty they even stabbed their horses to drink the blood. One or two in ten died.

sentences.zh: 榮定仰天太息，俄而澍雨，軍復振。

translations.literal: Rongding sighed to heaven; soon a timely rain fell and the army revived.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding sighed to heaven. Soon a timely rain fell and the army revived.

sentences.zh: 於是進擊，數挫其鋒，突厥憚之，請盟而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced to attack, repeatedly blunted their edge; the Turks feared him and requested alliance before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he advanced to attack and repeatedly blunted their edge. The Turks feared him, requested alliance, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賜縑萬匹，進爵安豐郡公，復封子憲為安康郡公，賜縑五千匹。

translations.literal: He was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, advanced to Duke of Anfeng Commandery, and his son Xian was again enfeoffed as Duke of Ankang Commandery with five thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, promoted to Duke of Anfeng Commandery, and his son Xian was again enfeoffed as Duke of Ankang Commandery with five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Grand General of the Right Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Grand General of the Right Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以為三公，榮定上書固辭，陳畏懼之道，帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him one of the Three Excellencies; Rongding submitted a memorial firmly declining and set forth the way of fear and caution, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make him one of the Three Excellencies. Rongding submitted a memorial firmly declining and set forth the way of fear and caution, and the emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards he received before and after were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝為之廢朝，令左衛大將軍元旻監護喪事，賻絹三千匹。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor suspended court for him, ordered Grand General of the Left Guard Yuan Min to supervise the funeral, and granted three thousand bolts of silk as funeral goods.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor suspended court, ordered Grand General of the Left Guard Yuan Min to supervise the funeral, and granted three thousand bolts of silk as funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「吾每欲致榮定於三事，其人固讓不可。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "I always wished to appoint Rongding to one of the Three Excellencies, but the man firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attendants, "I always wished to appoint Rongding to one of the Three Excellencies, but he firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 今欲賜之，重違其志。」

translations.literal: Now I wish to grant him honors, but that would again violate his wishes."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to grant him further honors, but that would again violate his wishes.

sentences.zh: 於是贈冀州刺史、陳國公，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously granted Governor of Ji Province and Duke of Chen State; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was posthumously granted Governor of Ji Province and Duke of Chen State, with the posthumous name Yi, "Virtuous."

sentences.zh: 子抗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 慶弟璡，亦工草隸，頗解鍾律。

translations.literal: Yan Qing's younger brother Jin was also skilled in cursive and clerical script and understood bell tones well.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing's younger brother Jin was also skilled in cursive and clerical script and understood bell tones well.

sentences.zh: 歷位潁川、南郡、扶風太守。

translations.literal: He successively held the positions of Governor of Yingchuan, Nan, and Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Governor of Yingchuan, Nan, and Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 毅性溫和，每以謹慎自守，又尚周文帝第五女襄陽公主，特為朝廷所委信，雖任兼出內，未嘗有矜惰之容，時人以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Yi was gentle by nature and always guarded himself with caution; he also married the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, Princess Xiangyang, and was especially trusted by the court. Although his duties extended both inside and outside the palace, he never showed a proud or lazy bearing, and people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was gentle by nature and always guarded himself with caution. He also married the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, Princess Xiangyang, and was especially trusted by the court. Although his duties extended both inside and outside the palace, he never showed a proud or lazy bearing, and people of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 子賢嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 賢字托賢，志業通敏，少知名。

translations.literal: Xian, courtesy name Tuoxian, was quick and perceptive in ambition and work and was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, courtesy name Tuoxian, was quick and perceptive in ambition and work and was known from youth.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，授使持節、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority and General with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority and General with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，襲爵神武公，除遷州刺史。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang he inherited the title of Duke of Shenwu and was appointed Governor of Qian Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he inherited the title of Duke of Shenwu and was appointed Governor of Qian Province.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭祥，字盛樂，其先與魏俱起，有乞伏者，為賀蘭莫何弗，因以為氏。

translations.literal: Helan Xiang, courtesy name Shengle; his ancestors rose together with Wei. There was one Qifu who served as Helan Mohefu, and from this the clan name was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Xiang, courtesy name Shengle, came from ancestors who rose together with Wei. One Qifu served as Helan Mohefu, and from this the clan name was taken.

sentences.zh: 後有以良家子鎮武川者，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Later one who as a son of a good family garrisoned Wuchuan made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Later an ancestor posted to garrison Wuchuan as a soldier from a respectable family settled there.

sentences.zh: 父初真，少知名，為鄉閭所重，尚文帝姊建安長公主。

translations.literal: His father Chuzhen was known from youth and respected by his home region; he married the elder sister of Emperor Wen, Princess Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuzhen was known from youth and respected in his home region. He married the elder sister of Emperor Wen, Princess Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，追贈太傅、柱國、常山郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祥年十一而孤，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: Xiang was orphaned at eleven and observed mourning according to the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was orphaned at eleven and observed mourning according to the rites.

sentences.zh: 長於舅氏，特為周文帝所愛，雖在戎旅，常博延儒生，教以書傳。

translations.literal: He grew up in his maternal uncle's household and was especially loved by Emperor Wen of Zhou; even while in the army he regularly gathered Confucian scholars and taught them the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in his maternal uncle's household and was especially loved by Emperor Wen of Zhou. Even while in the army he regularly gathered Confucian scholars and taught them the classics.

sentences.zh: 周文初入關，祥與晉公護俱在晉陽，後乃遣使迎致之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen first entered the passes, Xiang and Duke of Jin Hu were both in Jinyang; later envoys were sent to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen first entered the Guanzhong region, Xiang and Duke of Jin Hu were both in Jinyang. Later envoys were sent to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office robes he was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving office robes he was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 少有膽氣，志在立功。

translations.literal: From youth he had courage and spirit and aspired to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had courage and spirit and aspired to achieve merit.

sentences.zh: 尋擢補都督，恆居帳下。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted and appointed Commander, constantly staying in the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted and appointed Commander, constantly staying in the command tent.

sentences.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，又迎魏孝武，以前後功封撫夷縣伯。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Houmochen Yue and in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei; for his past and present merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of Houmochen Yue and in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei. For his past and present merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyi County.

sentences.zh: 仍從擊潼關，獲東魏將薛長儒，又攻回洛拔之。

translations.literal: He then followed in the attack on Tong Pass, captured the Eastern Wei general Xue Changru, and also attacked and took Huiluo.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed in the attack on Tong Pass, captured the Eastern Wei general Xue Changru, and also attacked and took Huiluo.

sentences.zh: 還拜左右直長，進爵為公。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Chief of the Left and Right Direct Guard and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was appointed Chief of the Left and Right Direct Guard and advanced in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，從周文與東魏戰於芒山，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong he followed Zhou Wen in battle against Eastern Wei at Mangshan and was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, and additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong he followed Emperor Wen in battle against Eastern Wei at Mangshan and was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and additionally appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除都督、荊州刺史，進爵博陵郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Commander and Governor of Jing Province and advanced to Duke of Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Commander and Governor of Jing Province and promoted to Duke of Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 先是祥嘗行荊州事，雖未期月，頗有惠政，至是重往，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Previously Xiang had temporarily administered Jing Province affairs; although not a full month, he had benevolent policies; when he went again on this occasion, the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Xiang had temporarily administered Jing Province affairs. Although not a full month had passed, he had already shown benevolent policies. When he returned on this occasion, the common people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 由是漢南流人繈負至者，日有千數，還近蠻夷莫不款附。

translations.literal: Thereupon refugees south of the Han came carrying infants on their backs at a rate of a thousand per day, and nearby barbarians all submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon refugees south of the Han came carrying infants on their backs at a rate of a thousand per day, and nearby barbarians all submitted in good faith.

sentences.zh: 祥隨機撫納，咸得其歡心。

translations.literal: Xiang according to circumstances comforted and received them, and all won his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang comforted and received them according to circumstances, and all won his favor.

sentences.zh: 時盛夏亢陽，祥親巡境內，觀政得失，見有發掘古塚，暴露骸骨，乃謂守令曰：「此豈仁者為政邪！」

translations.literal: At that time in midsummer there was severe drought; Xiang personally toured within the borders to observe the gains and losses of government, saw ancient tombs being excavated and bones exposed, and said to the governors and magistrates: "Is this the government of a benevolent man!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time in midsummer there was severe drought. Xiang personally toured within the borders to observe the gains and losses of government, saw ancient tombs being excavated and bones exposed, and said to the governors and magistrates, "Is this the government of a benevolent man!

sentences.zh: 命所在收葬之。

translations.literal: He ordered that they be collected and buried wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that they be collected and buried wherever found.

sentences.zh: 即日澍雨，是歲大有年。

translations.literal: That very day a timely rain fell and that year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: That very day a timely rain fell and that year there was a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 境內多古墓，其俗好行發掘，至是遂息。

translations.literal: Within the borders there were many ancient tombs and the custom favored tomb-robbing; from this time it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Within the borders there were many ancient tombs and the custom favored tomb-robbing. From this time it ceased.

sentences.zh: 祥雖周文密親，性甚清素。

translations.literal: Although Xiang was a close intimate of Zhou Wen, his nature was very pure and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiang was a close intimate of Emperor Wen, his nature was very pure and plain.

sentences.zh: 州境南接襄陽，西通岷蜀，物產所出，多諸珍異。

translations.literal: The province bordered Xiangyang in the south and connected to Min and Shu in the west; the products of the land included many rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Xiangyang in the south and connected to Min and Shu in the west, and the products of the land included many rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 既與梁通好，行李往來，公私贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: Since friendly relations had been established with Liang, travelers came and went and public and private gifts were exchanged, but he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Since friendly relations had been established with Liang, travelers came and went and public and private gifts were exchanged, but he accepted none of them.

sentences.zh: 梁雍州刺史、岳陽王蕭詧欽其風素，乃以竹屏風、絺綌之屬及經史贈之。

translations.literal: Xiao Cha, Prince of Yueyang and Governor of Yong Province of Liang, admired his integrity and therefore sent him bamboo screens, fine hemp cloth, and the like along with classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha, Prince of Yueyang and Governor of Yong Province of Liang, admired his integrity and sent him bamboo screens, fine hemp cloth, and the like along with classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 祥難違其意，取而付諸所司。

translations.literal: Xiang found it hard to go against his intent and took the gifts and handed them over to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang found it hard to go against his intent and handed the gifts over to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 周文後聞之，並以賜祥。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen later heard of this, he gave them all to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen later heard of this, he gave them all to Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 周文以涇、渭溉灌之處，渠堰廢毀，乃令祥修造富平堰，開渠引水，東注於洛。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen, because the irrigation areas of Jing and Wei had ruined canals and dikes, ordered Xiang to repair and build the Fuping Weir, open a canal to draw water, and channel it east into the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Because the irrigation areas of the Jing and Wei rivers had ruined canals and dikes, Emperor Wen ordered Xiang to repair and build the Fuping Weir, open a canal to draw water, and channel it east into the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 功用既畢，人獲其利。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, the people gained its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed, the people reaped its benefits.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，行華州事，後改華州為同州，仍以祥為刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he administered Hua Province affairs; later Hua Province was renamed Tong Province and Xiang was still made its governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he administered Hua Province affairs. Later Hua Province was renamed Tong Province and Xiang remained its governor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Left in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Director of the Left in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授小司馬。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Junior Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Junior Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進位柱國、大司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was advanced to Pillar of the State and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was promoted to Pillar of the State and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，祥與護中表，少相親愛，軍國之事，護皆與祥參謀。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Xiang and Hu were maternal cousins and from youth had been close; in matters of army and state Hu always consulted with Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duke of Jin Hu held power. Xiang and Hu were maternal cousins and had been close since youth. In matters of army and state Hu always consulted with Xiang.

sentences.zh: 及誅趙貴，廢閔帝，祥有力焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao Gui was executed and Emperor Min was deposed, Xiang had a strong hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Gui was executed and Emperor Min was deposed, Xiang played an important part.

sentences.zh: 武成初，吐谷渾侵掠州郡，詔祥與宇文貴總兵討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng the Tuyuhun raided and plundered prefectures and commanderies; an edict ordered Xiang and Yuwen Gui to command troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng the Tuyuhun raided and plundered prefectures and commanderies. An edict ordered Xiang and Yuwen Gui to command troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 祥乃遣其軍司檄吐谷渾，與渾廣定王、鍾留王等戰，破之，因拔其洮陽、洪和二城，以其地為洮州。

translations.literal: Xiang then sent his army secretary to issue a proclamation to the Tuyuhun and fought with Prince Guangding and Prince Zhongliu of the Tuyuhun, defeating them; he then took their cities of Taoyang and Honghe and made the territory Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then sent his army secretary to issue a proclamation to the Tuyuhun and fought Prince Guangding and Prince Zhongliu of the Tuyuhun, defeating them. He then took their cities of Taoyang and Honghe and made the territory Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 撫安西土，振旅而還。

translations.literal: He comforted and settled the western lands and returned with his army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted and settled the western lands and returned with his army in good order.

sentences.zh: 進封涼國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Liang State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Liang State.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太師、同岐等十三州諸軍事、同州刺史，諡曰景。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Commander of Military Affairs in Thirteen Provinces including Tong and Qi, and Governor of Tong Province; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Commander of Military Affairs in Thirteen Provinces including Tong and Qi, and Governor of Tong Province, with the posthumous name Jing, "Illustrious."

sentences.zh: 有七子，敬、讓、璨、師、寬知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Jing, Rang, Can, Shi, and Kuan were well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Jing, Rang, Can, Shi, and Kuan were well known.

sentences.zh: 敬少曆顯職，封化隆縣侯，後襲爵涼國公。

translations.literal: Jing from youth held prominent offices, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hualong County, and later inherited the title of Duke of Liang State.
translations.idiomatic: Jing from youth held prominent offices, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hualong County, and later inherited the title of Duke of Liang State.

sentences.zh: 位柱國、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the positions of Pillar of the State and Governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Pillar of the State and Governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 讓，大將軍、鄭州刺史、河東郡公。

translations.literal: Rang was Grand General, Governor of Zheng Province, and Duke of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rang served as Grand General, Governor of Zheng Province, and Duke of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 璨，開府儀同三司、宣陽郡公。

translations.literal: Can was Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Xunyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Can was Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Xunyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 建德五年，從于并州戰歿，贈上儀同大將軍，追封清都公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande he followed the campaign at Bing Province and died in battle; posthumously granted Senior General with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande he followed the campaign at Bing Province and died in battle. He was posthumously granted Senior General with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 師，尚明帝女，位上儀同大將軍、幽州刺史、博陵郡公。

translations.literal: Shi married a daughter of Emperor Ming and held the positions of Senior General with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of You Province, and Duke of Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi married a daughter of Emperor Ming and served as Senior General with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of You Province, and Duke of Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 寬，開府儀同大將軍、武始公。

translations.literal: Kuan was Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Wushi.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Wushi.

sentences.zh: 入隋，曆汴、鄭二州刺史，並著政績。

translations.literal: Under Sui he successively served as Governor of Bian and Zheng Provinces, both with notable administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he successively served as Governor of Bian and Zheng Provinces, both with notable administrative achievements.

sentences.zh: 祥弟隆，大將軍、襄樂縣公。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Long was Grand General and Duke of Xiangle County.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's younger brother Long was Grand General and Duke of Xiangle County.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝與祥有舊，開皇初，追贈上柱國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui had old ties with Xiang; at the beginning of Kaihuang he was posthumously granted Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui had old ties with Xiang. At the beginning of Kaihuang he was posthumously granted Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 叱列伏龜，字摩頭陀，代郡西部人也。

translations.literal: Chiliefu Gui, courtesy name Motuotuo, was a man of the western part of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chiliefu Gui, courtesy name Motuotuo, was a native of the western part of Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先為部落大人，魏初入附，遂世為第一領人酋長，至龜五世。

translations.literal: His ancestors were tribal chieftains; when Wei first submitted and attached themselves, they thus for generations were the first-ranking tribal chieftains down to Gui's fifth generation.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were tribal chieftains. When Wei first submitted and attached themselves, they served for generations as first-ranking tribal chieftains down to Gui's fifth generation.

sentences.zh: 龜容貌瑰偉，腰帶十圍，進止詳雅，兼有武藝。

translations.literal: Gui had a magnificent appearance, a waist girdle ten arm-spans around, dignified bearing in advancing and stopping, and also possessed martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had a magnificent appearance, a waist girdle ten arm-spans around, dignified bearing in advancing and stopping, and also possessed martial skill.

sentences.zh: 嗣父業復為領人酋長。

translations.literal: He succeeded his father's estate and again became tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded his father's estate and again became tribal chieftain.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌三年，以別將從長孫承業西征，累遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang of Wei, as a separate commander he followed Changsun Chengye on the western campaign and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Gold Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaochang of Wei, as a separate commander he followed Changsun Chengye on the western campaign and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Gold Seal.

sentences.zh: 從還洛，授都督，遂為齊神武所寵任，加授大都督。

translations.literal: On return to Luoyang he was appointed Commander and then was favored and trusted by Gao Huan of Qi, additionally granted Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On return to Luoyang he was appointed Commander and then was favored and trusted by Gao Huan of Qi, additionally granted Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，隨例來降。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Shayuan he came over in surrender according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Shayuan he came over in surrender according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 周文帝以其豪門，解縛禮之，仍以邵惠公女妻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because he was from a great house, released his bonds and honored him, and moreover gave him the daughter of Duke of Shao in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because he was from a great house, released his bonds and honored him, and gave him the daughter of Duke of Shao in marriage.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，封長樂縣公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changle County.

sentences.zh: 自此常從征討，亟有戰功。

translations.literal: From this time he constantly followed on campaigns and repeatedly had military merit.
translations.idiomatic: From this time he constantly followed on campaigns and repeatedly won military merit.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the positions of Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，子椿嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Chun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died. His son Chun succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 椿字千年。

translations.literal: Chun, courtesy name Qiannian.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, courtesy name Qiannian.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，改封永世縣公。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming he held the positions of General of Agile Cavalry and Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yongshi County.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Ming he served as General of Agile Cavalry and Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yongshi County.

sentences.zh: 天和初，除左宮伯，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was appointed Left Palace Attendant and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianhe he was appointed Left Palace Attendant and promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 閻慶，字仁度，河陰人也。

translations.literal: Yan Qing, courtesy name Rendu, was a man of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing, courtesy name Rendu, was a native of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖善，仕魏曆龍驤將軍、雲州鎮將，因家雲州之盛樂郡。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shan served Wei and successively held the positions of General of Agile Dragon and Garrison Commander of Yun Province, making his home in Shengle Commandery of Yun Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shan served Wei and successively held the positions of General of Agile Dragon and Garrison Commander of Yun Province, settling in Shengle Commandery of Yun Province.

sentences.zh: 祖提，持節、車騎大將軍、敦煌鎮都大將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ti was Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand General of Dunhuang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ti was Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand General of Dunhuang Garrison.

sentences.zh: 父進，有謀略，勇冠當時。

translations.literal: His father Jin had stratagems and his courage surpassed his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin had stratagems and his courage surpassed his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 正光中，拜龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: In Zhenguang he was appointed General of Agile Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguang he was appointed General of Agile Dragon.

sentences.zh: 屬衛可瑰作亂，攻圍盛樂，進率眾拒守，以功拜盛樂郡守。

translations.literal: When Wei Kei rebelled and besieged Shengle, Jin led the masses to resist and defend; for his merit he was appointed Governor of Shengle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Kei rebelled and besieged Shengle, Jin led the masses to resist and defend. For his merit he was appointed Governor of Shengle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 慶幼聰敏，重然諾，風儀端肅，望之儼然。

translations.literal: Qing from youth was clever and keen, valued his promises, and his bearing was dignified and solemn; viewed from afar he inspired awe.
translations.idiomatic: Qing from youth was clever and keen, valued his promises, and carried himself with dignified solemnity that inspired awe from afar.

sentences.zh: 隨父因守盛樂，頗有力焉，拜別將。

translations.literal: Following his father in defending Shengle he was quite effective and was appointed Separate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Following his father in defending Shengle he was quite effective and was appointed Separate Commander.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功拜步兵校尉、中堅將軍。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was appointed Colonel of Foot Soldiers and General of the Central Firmament.
translations.idiomatic: Later for military merit he was appointed Colonel of Foot Soldiers and General of the Central Firmament.

sentences.zh: 既而齊神武舉兵入洛，魏孝武西遷，慶謂所親曰：「高歡將有篡逆之謀，豈可苟安目前，受其控制也？」

translations.literal: Before long Gao Huan of Qi raised troops and entered Luoyang; Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west; Qing said to those close to him: "Gao Huan will have usurping and rebellious designs—how can one seek temporary ease and accept his control?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Huan raised troops and entered Luoyang and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west. Qing said to those close to him, "Gao Huan will have usurping and rebellious designs. How can one seek temporary ease and accept his control?

sentences.zh: 遂以大統三年自宜陽歸闕。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the third year of Datong he returned to court from Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon in the third year of Datong he returned to court from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷後將軍，封安次縣子，以功進爵為伯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Rear General, enfeoffed as Viscount of Anci County, and for merit advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Rear General, enfeoffed as Viscount of Anci County, and for merit advanced in rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 慶善於綏撫，士卒未休，未嘗先舍，故能盡其死力，屢獲勳勞。

translations.literal: Qing was good at comforting and settling; when the soldiers had not yet rested he never rested first, and therefore could exhaust their utmost strength and repeatedly gain merit and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was good at comforting and settling his men. When the soldiers had not yet rested he never rested first, and therefore could draw their utmost strength and repeatedly gain merit and honor.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、雲州大中正，加侍中，賜姓大野氏。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, Chief Rectifier of Yun Province, additionally made Palace Attendant, and granted the surname Daye.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Chief Rectifier of Yun Province, additionally appointed Palace Attendant, and granted the surname Daye.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，出為河州刺史，進爵石保縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he went out as Governor of He Province and was advanced to Duke of Shibao County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was posted as Governor of He Province and promoted to Duke of Shibao County.

sentences.zh: 州居河外，地接戎夷，慶留心撫納，頗稱簡惠。

translations.literal: The province lay beyond the Yellow River and bordered the Rong barbarians; Qing devoted attention to comforting and receiving them and was praised for simplicity and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay beyond the Yellow River and bordered the Rong barbarians. Qing devoted attention to comforting and receiving them and was praised for simplicity and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 就拜大將軍，進爵太安郡公。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke of Tai'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand General and promoted to Duke of Tai'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為小司空，曆雲、甯二州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Junior Minister of Works and successively served as Governor of Yun and Ning Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Junior Minister of Works and successively served as Governor of Yun and Ning Provinces.

sentences.zh: 慶性寬和，不苛察，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: Qing was by nature broad and harmonious and not harsh in scrutiny; the common people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was broad and harmonious by nature and not harsh in scrutiny. The common people were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was advanced to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was promoted to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 晉公護母，慶之姑也。

translations.literal: The mother of Duke of Jin Hu was Qing's paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Duke of Jin Hu was Qing's paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 護雖擅朝，而慶未嘗阿附。

translations.literal: Although Hu monopolized the court, Qing never fawned upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Hu monopolized the court, Qing never fawned upon him.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，武帝以此重之。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Emperor Wu valued him all the more for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was executed, Emperor Wu valued him all the more for this.

sentences.zh: 詔慶第十二子毗尚帝女清都公主。

translations.literal: An edict had Qing's twelfth son Pi marry Princess Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Qing's twelfth son Pi marry Princess Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 慶雖位望隆重，婚連帝室，常以廉慎自守，時以此稱之。

translations.literal: Although Qing's rank and standing were exalted and his marriage connected to the imperial house, he always guarded himself with integrity and caution, and people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Although Qing's rank and standing were exalted and his marriage connected to the imperial house, he always guarded himself with integrity and caution, and people of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，抗表致事，優詔許焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and a gracious edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 慶既衰老，恆嬰沉痼。

translations.literal: Qing was already aged and constantly suffered from chronic illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was already aged and constantly suffered from chronic illness.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以其先朝耆舊，特異恆倫，乃詔靜帝至第問疾。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, because he was an elder of the former dynasty, made an exception to ordinary propriety and ordered Emperor Jing to visit his residence to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, because he was an elder of the former dynasty, made an exception to ordinary propriety and ordered Emperor Jing to visit his residence to inquire after his illness.

sentences.zh: 賜布千段，醫藥所須，令有司供給。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand bolts of cloth and whatever medicine was needed, with orders to the relevant offices to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a thousand bolts of cloth and whatever medicine was needed, with orders to the relevant offices to supply them.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was appointed Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang he was appointed Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，又令皇太子就第問疾，仍供醫藥之費。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he again ordered the crown prince to visit his residence to inquire after his illness and continued to supply medical expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he again ordered the crown prince to visit his residence to inquire after his illness and continued to supply medical expenses.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年薨，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Kaihuang at age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kaihuang at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、七州諸軍事、荊州刺史，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works, Commander of Military Affairs in Seven Provinces, and Governor of Jing Province; posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works, Commander of Military Affairs in Seven Provinces, and Governor of Jing Province, with the posthumous name Cheng, "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 長子常，先慶卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Chang died before Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Chang died before Qing.

sentences.zh: 次子毗嗣。

translations.literal: The second son Pi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Pi succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 毗，七歲襲爵石保縣公。

translations.literal: Pi at age seven inherited the title of Duke of Shibao County.
translations.idiomatic: Pi at age seven inherited the title of Duke of Shibao County.

sentences.zh: 及長，儀貌矜嚴，頗好經史，受漢書于蕭該，略通大旨。

translations.literal: When he grew up his bearing was stern and dignified; he greatly loved the classics and histories and studied the Book of Han under Xiao Gai, gaining a general understanding of its main points.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up his bearing was stern and dignified. He greatly loved the classics and histories and studied the Book of Han under Xiao Gai, gaining a general understanding of its main points.

sentences.zh: 能篆書，草隸尤善，為當時之妙。

translations.literal: He could write seal script and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script, the finest of his age.
translations.idiomatic: He could write seal script and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script, the finest of his age.

sentences.zh: 周武帝見而悅之，命尚清都公主。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and was pleased, ordering him to marry Princess Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and was pleased, ordering him to marry Princess Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Pi was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Pi was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，以技藝侍東宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he served the Eastern Palace with his artistic skills.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui founded the dynasty, he served the Eastern Palace with his artistic skills.

sentences.zh: 數以琱麗之物取悅于皇太子，由是甚見親待，每稱之於上。

translations.literal: He repeatedly used ornate carved objects to please the crown prince and thereby was greatly favored and treated; he was often praised to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly used ornate carved objects to please the crown prince and thereby was greatly favored. He was often praised to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜車騎，宿衛東宮。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of Chariots and Cavalry and guarded the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand Master of Chariots and Cavalry and guarded the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上嘗遣高熲大閱于龍台澤，諸軍部伍多不齊整，唯毗一軍，法制肅然。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent Gao Jiong to conduct a great review at Longtai Marsh; the formations of many armies were disorderly, but Pi's army alone was disciplined and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent Gao Jiong to conduct a great review at Longtai Marsh. The formations of many armies were disorderly, but Pi's army alone was disciplined and orderly.

sentences.zh: 熲言之於上，特蒙賜制。

translations.literal: Jiong reported this to the emperor and Pi was specially granted an imperial composition.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong reported this to the emperor and Pi was specially granted an imperial composition.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太子宗衛率長史，尋加上儀同。

translations.literal: Before long he additionally served as Chief Administrator of the Crown Prince's Ancestral Guard Command and was soon granted Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he additionally served as Chief Administrator of the Crown Prince's Ancestral Guard Command and was soon granted Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太子服玩之物多毗所為。

translations.literal: Many of the crown prince's garments and playthings were made by Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the crown prince's garments and playthings were made by Pi.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，毗坐杖一百，與妻子俱配為官奴婢。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, Pi was sentenced to one hundred strokes of the cane and he and his wife and children were all assigned as official slaves.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, Pi was sentenced to one hundred strokes of the cane and he and his wife and children were all assigned as official slaves.

sentences.zh: 二歲放免。

translations.literal: After two years they were released and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After two years they were released and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，盛修軍器，以毗性巧，練習舊事，詔典其職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne he greatly expanded military equipment; because Pi was clever by nature and practiced in old affairs, an edict put him in charge of this duty.
